It should not be part of the default shape family unless validation shows it helps.

docs.title: Reference-Calibrated Mode
docs.text:
Reference-calibrated rejection should compare each class average against a library of projected reference signatures.

Reference-library generation can reuse the existing reproject command rather than projecting volumes inside model_cavgs_rejection at first. A user would produce a stack of model projections over a sufficiently dense angular grid, using the appropriate symmetry, mask diameter, sampling distance, contrast, and box size. The rejection backend would then read that stack and compute the same shape signatures.

Recommended comparison strategy:

  • Compute a normalized distance-transform histogram for every reference projection.
  • Compute PCA aspect ratio, compactness, area fraction, and topology metrics for every reference projection.
  • For each class average, compute the nearest or low-percentile distance to the reference library rather than applying independent min/max bounds to every feature.
  • Use robust reference statistics: median, MAD, percentile envelopes, or nearest-reference distances.
  • Convert distances into quality-oriented scalar features, for example shape_ref_score = -robust_z(distance_to_reference_library), so larger values mean closer to expected model geometry.

Good histogram distances for this use case:

  • 1D Wasserstein distance, implemented as the sum of absolute cumulative histogram differences.
  • Chi-squared distance with a small epsilon for empty bins.
  • Hellinger or Jensen-Shannon distance, already conceptually aligned with normalized histograms.

For shape vectors, avoid raw min/max gates as the primary decision. A Mahalanobis distance in a low-dimensional descriptor space, a robust nearest neighbor distance, or a percentile envelope over the final scalar distance is preferable.

docs.title: Phase 0: Documentation and Validation Targets
docs.text:
Define the exact descriptors, feature names, output tables, and validation criteria before code changes.

Acceptance criteria for this phase:

  • clear distinction between reference-free shape descriptors and reference-calibrated shape scores;
  • agreement that shape evidence starts as analysis/learn evidence, not as a hard reject;
  • decision on whether initial reference support accepts a projection stack only or also accepts a volume directly;
  • expected output files and analysis columns named.

docs.title: Phase 1: Shape Helper Design
docs.text:
Introduce a small shape-analysis helper owned by src/main/cavg_quality.

Planned responsibilities:

  • build or receive the cleaned foreground mask;
  • compute foreground area, centroid, component count, and hole metrics;
  • compute the exact 2D Euclidean distance transform;
  • build a normalized distance-transform histogram;
  • compute scalar shape descriptors;
  • expose reference-library comparison helpers.

Keeping this helper under src/main/cavg_quality is lower risk than adding a general image API immediately. If other subsystems later need distance transforms, the helper can be promoted into src/main/image.

docs.title: Phase 2: Feature-Bank Integration
docs.text:
Add a shape evidence family to the quality feature bank.

Required updates:

  • increase the feature count in simple_cavg_quality_types.f90;
  • add feature indices and definitions in simple_cavg_quality_feats.f90;
  • compute shape features from the cleaned foreground mask;
  • update built-in weight arrays in simple_cavg_quality_model.f90;
  • preserve existing built-in behavior by assigning zero shape weights to current defaults;
  • bump model-file and analysis-table versions;
  • support reading older model files by padding missing new weights with zero, or explicitly require retraining for shape-aware models;
  • update simple_cavg_quality_analysis.f90 so raw and normalized shape columns appear in analysis and feature tables;
  • update simple_cavg_quality_learn.f90 so feature-policy search can include shape-aware policies.

Feature-policy options should stay small. A reasonable first set is:

  • current policies unchanged;
  • microchunk_plus_shape;
  • microchunk_plus_score_shape;
  • microchunk_plus_score_signal_shape.

The default model should not silently start rejecting more classes because shape features exist. Shape-aware rejection should require a learned model, a promoted model, or an explicit reference-calibrated score.

docs.title: Phase 3: Reference Library Support
docs.text:
Add optional reference-stack support to model_cavgs_rejection.

Recommended first interface:

  • user supplies a reference projection stack;
  • backend computes reference shape signatures at apply/analyze time;
  • backend emits a reference summary file;
  • backend adds a scalar reference-closeness feature to the shape family.

Possible future interface:

  • user supplies vol1, nspace, pgrp, and mskdiam;
  • backend invokes or reuses the existing reprojection machinery internally.

The projection-stack interface is preferable for the first implementation because it keeps volume projection, contrast handling, masking, and orientation sampling outside the rejection backend.

docs.title: Phase 4: Diagnostics and Outputs
docs.text:
Analysis output should make shape behavior inspectable.

Recommended outputs:

  • raw and normalized shape columns in the main analysis table;
  • per-feature AUC, robust separation, current weight, and suggested weight, as already done for current features;
  • optional cavgs_shape_reference_summary.txt with reference-library descriptor distributions, histogram-distance percentiles, and outlier counts;
  • optional cavgs_shape_features.txt if the shape signature contains more detail than the compact model feature columns can show;
  • selected/rejected stacks unchanged.

The report should explicitly distinguish:

  • hard rejects caused by existing validity gates;
  • soft rejects from the learned model;
  • classes whose shape score is outside the reference envelope;
  • classes where segmentation failed or produced degenerate shape descriptors.

docs.title: Phase 5: Validation
docs.text:
Validation should happen before any shape-aware built-in model is promoted.

Synthetic tests:

  • small binary masks with known distance-transform values;
  • discs, rectangles, rings, and two-component masks;
  • invariance under 90-degree rotations and approximate stability under interpolated in-plane rotations;
  • compactness and aspect-ratio sanity checks.

Reference-projection tests:

  • use SIMPLE's existing reproject path to generate projections of a known volume;
  • verify that projected references fall inside their own reference distribution;
  • verify that obvious synthetic junk masks fall outside;
  • test contrast and mask-radius sensitivity.

Manual-data validation:

  • run quality_mode=analyze on existing manually selected projects;
  • compare current defaults against shape-aware learned candidates;
  • inspect false positives and false negatives with selected/rejected stacks;
  • check whether shape evidence removes junk aggregates without rejecting legitimate rare projections;
  • compare chunk and pool contexts separately.

Promotion criteria:

  • shape-aware model improves balanced accuracy or false-positive rejection on multiple datasets;
  • manually good hard rejects do not increase;
  • gains survive leave-one-dataset-out diagnostics;
  • behavior remains stable when no reference stack is supplied.

docs.title: Phase 6: Optional Stream Integration
docs.text:
Only after batch/analyze validation should stream integration be considered.

The stream and sieve paths already evaluate the cavg_quality backend (sieve, chunk and pool contexts). A future stream integration should decide whether to:

  • add the shape evidence to the stream contexts' feature vectors;
  • call only the shape helper as an extra hard gate in a stream context;
  • reserve shape evidence for batch/pool cleanup.

This decision should account for stream sentinels, chunk lifecycle, selected and rejected stack writing, particle-state propagation, and retry behavior.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
• Should the first implementation expose only a reference projection stack, or should it also accept a volume and generate projections internally?
  • What distance normalization is most stable across projects: mask radius, equivalent-disc radius, or mskdiam / smpd?
  • Should aspect ratio be a diagnostic-only descriptor unless a reference model is present?
  • How should multi-state references be represented: one combined projection library, state-specific libraries, or best score over all states?
  • How much hole filling should be applied before the distance transform, and should hole metrics be computed before or after cleanup?
  • Should shape features be unavailable when the foreground mask area is too small but not already hard rejected?
  • Are there target classes where compactness penalizes true projections, such as elongated complexes, filaments, or membrane-associated particles?

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Distance-transform shape evidence is worth pursuing for SIMPLE, but it should be introduced as a measured extension of the existing class-average quality model. The safest path is to reuse the current segmentation machinery, add rotation-invariant shape diagnostics, validate them through quality_mode=analyze and quality_mode=learn, then add reference-calibrated scoring using projection stacks generated by the existing reprojection workflow.

The most important design rule is to avoid turning raw geometric descriptors into hard rejection gates too early. Shape should first become inspectable, learnable evidence; only validated reference-calibrated distances should become strong rejection signals.

docs.title: Joint 2D/3D Latent Affinity Propagation
docs.text: Date: July 21, 2026 Status: Concise implementation proposal

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Combine two particle-level descriptions of conformational variation:

  • local 2D diffusion coordinates from groups of nearby projection directions;
  • global 3D coordinates and uncertainties from flex_analysis.

The result should be one conformational label per particle and one validated 3D map per state. SIMPLE's existing affinity-propagation (AP) implementation should perform the clustering.

docs.title: Core Idea
docs.text:
Use AP twice:

2D diffusion coordinates + 3D flex coordinates
                    |
          local AP in each angular patch
                    |
          view-specific particle exemplars
                    |
       global AP over the local exemplars
                    |
       states containing exemplars from many views
                    |
             state-specific 3D maps

The first pass detects conformational structure where projections are directly comparable. The second pass identifies which local clusters represent the same 3D state.

docs.title: Terminology
docs.text:
Three different objects must not be confused:

  • Orientation bin: an atomic, disjoint projection-direction assignment. Each particle has one orientation bin.
  • Angular patch: a temporary neighborhood made from several nearby bins. Patches overlap so neighboring analyses share particles.
  • Conformational state: the final global AP cluster. Each particle has one hard state label.

For example:

orientation bins:      A   B   C   D   E

patch centered at B:  [A   B   C]
patch centered at C:      [B   C   D]
patch centered at D:          [C   D   E]

A particle in bin C is analyzed in three local diffusion charts. It may have three local coordinate vectors and three temporary local labels, but it still has one orientation and one final conformational state.

The project stores the particle once. Patch membership is represented by particle-index lists, so images need not be duplicated. When evidence from overlapping patches is combined, per-particle patch weights satisfy

sum[g in G_i] omega_ig = 1

and the particle is counted once in reconstruction.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
For particle i:

  • m_i: canonical flex_analysis coordinate;
  • S_i: posterior covariance of m_i;
  • u_ig: diffusion coordinate in angular patch g;
  • pind_i: stable project particle index.

The flex_analysis basis volumes B_q and consensus map V_mean are also required to map state coordinates back to volumes.

All joins use project particle index, never row order.

docs.title: 1. Build Overlapping Angular Patches
docs.text:
Use the existing projection grid as patch centers. Each patch contains its center bin and nearby orientation bins.

Within a patch:

  1. align/transport particles to the patch center;
  2. subtract the projected consensus map;
  3. use the same CTF/noise convention as flex_analysis;
  4. construct a diffusion map from the residual images.

Orientation should select candidate neighbors, but residual-image similarity should determine graph weights. The current ptcl3D default graph=ori weights edges using orientation distance alone and therefore describes viewing geometry rather than conformation. Until a hybrid graph exists, graph=euc on properly transformed residual images is the better starting point.

Persist each chart's particle indices, coordinates, eigenvalues, graph diagnostics, and patch weights. Do not immediately discard the coordinates after local clustering.

docs.title: 2. Local Joint Affinity Propagation
docs.text:
For particles i and j in patch g, combine normalized 2D and 3D distances:

D_g(i,j) = alpha_2 D_2g(i,j) + alpha_3 D_3(i,j)
  • D_2g is diffusion distance inside patch g.
  • D_3 is a distance between flex_analysis coordinates, preferably using S_i + S_j so uncertain particles contribute less strongly.

Run the existing AP wrapper:

call cluster_dmat(D_g, 'aprop', nlocal, centers, labels, ap_pref=pref)

Use the median off-diagonal similarity as the initial preference. Retain:

  • the exemplar particle index;
  • local member particle indices;
  • patch identifier;
  • preference and similarity sum;
  • 3D mean/covariance of the local members.

Each local AP cluster is now a meta-item for the global pass.

docs.title: 3. Global Affinity Propagation
docs.text:
Compare local exemplars a and b using:

D_meta(a,b) = beta_3 D_3cluster(a,b)
            + beta_o H_ab [1 - overlap_agreement(a,b)]
  • D_3cluster compares their member distributions in the global 3D latent space.
  • overlap_agreement measures whether particles shared by the two patches retain the same local membership.
  • H_ab is zero when the patches have insufficient overlap, making missing overlap evidence neutral.

Run AP on D_meta. Its output maps every local exemplar to a global conformational state.

A global state is therefore an angular atlas of view-specific exemplars. The single meta-exemplar selected by AP identifies the cluster, but final particle assignment uses the state's complete exemplar set rather than only that one view.

docs.title: 4. Assign Particles and Create 3D Maps
docs.text:
Map each particle's local AP labels through the global exemplar labels. If overlapping patches disagree, resolve the assignment using the closest available state exemplars plus the particle's 3D coordinate.

The baseline output is one hard AP state per particle. An optional soft weight may be derived from the final state-distance margin for reconstruction, but it must be described as a similarity weight, not a Bayesian posterior.

For state k, calculate its mean 3D latent coordinate mu_k and form the fast eigenvolume prediction:

V_k = V_mean + sum_q mu_k(q) B_q

Then reconstruct even/odd maps directly from particles assigned to the state. The particle reconstructions are the physical validation target; the eigenvolume maps are model predictions.

docs.title: Why Two AP Passes?
docs.text:
A single AP pass over all particles is unsuitable because:

  1. diffusion coordinates are comparable only inside their own angular patch;
  2. one particle exemplar represents only one projection direction;
  3. the existing AP implementation uses dense N x N matrices.

The two-pass design keeps local comparisons valid, represents each state with many viewing directions, and confines dense AP matrices to patches and the much smaller exemplar set.

The current aff_prop object stores seven dense real matrices. Through cluster_dmat, the input distance and converted similarity matrices are also live. A conservative memory estimate is therefore at least

36 * N * N bytes

per AP call. Check this before allocation and fail clearly when a patch or meta-exemplar set is too large.

docs.title: Selecting the Number of States
docs.text:
AP determines cluster count through its diagonal preference:

  • start with the existing median-similarity preference;
  • scan a small range of global preference quantiles;
  • record preference, exemplar count, convergence warning, and similarity sum;
  • select the simplest solution stable across half-sets and angular holdouts.

Do not normally use nclust_max: the current wrapper enforces that limit with a k-medoids merge, so the final result would no longer be a pure AP solution.

docs.title: Reuse
docs.text:
• simple_aff_prop.f90: existing AP message passing and deterministic tie-breaking;
  • simple_clustering_utils.f90: cluster_dmat(..., 'aprop', ...) and AP preference handling;
  • simple_projected_latent_result.f90: in-memory particle indices, z, posterior covariance, residuals, and mode variances.

docs.title: Add or Refactor
docs.text:
• simple_cls_split_strategy.f90
  • separate diffusion embedding from k-medoids;
  • return non-destructive, particle-indexed local charts;
  • generate overlapping angular patches.
  • simple_diff_map_graphs.f90
  • add orientation-gated, residual-image-weighted affinities.
  • simple_projected_latent_result.f90
  • serialize posterior covariance as well as coordinates.
  • new simple_joint_latent_aff_prop.f90
  • joint distances;
  • local and global AP;
  • preference scans;
  • final assignments and diagnostics.
  • new high-level flex_map3D workflow
  • orchestrate features, AP, mapping, reconstruction, and validation.

The existing AP API may need small additions to expose convergence status, memory estimates, or per-item preferences. The clustering algorithm itself does not need to be replaced.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
flex_map3D_particles.txt
    particle, z..., state, assignment_margin, optional_weights..., residual

flex_map3D_exemplars.txt
    exemplar_particle, patch, local_population, global_state

flex_map3D_states.txt
    state, population, z_centroid..., validation_metrics

flex_map3D_patches.txt
    patch, population, rank, AP_preference, exemplar_count, overlap_consistency

flex_map3D_stateNN_eigenvol.mrc
flex_map3D_stateNN_even.mrc
flex_map3D_stateNN_odd.mrc

Preserve existing project class fields by default, and never overload the record-activation state field. Updating project assignments must be explicit.

docs.title: Minimal Implementation Sequence
docs.text:
1. Preserve/export local diffusion charts and flex_analysis covariance.
  2. Implement local joint AP and write exemplars without changing the project.
  3. Implement global exemplar AP and final particle labels.
  4. Write eigenvolume-predicted maps.
  5. Reconstruct and validate even/odd state maps.
  6. Add preference scanning and optional similarity-weighted reconstruction.

docs.title: Required Validation
docs.text:
• known-state simulation with realistic orientations, CTFs, and noise;
  • homogeneous null data, which must not yield reproducible state differences;
  • even/odd reproducibility of state assignments and maps;
  • angular holdout and patch-dropout stability;
  • 2D-only, 3D-only, and joint-distance ablation;
  • repeated AP runs with identical exemplars and convergence;
  • comparison of eigenvolume-predicted maps with particle reconstructions.

docs.title: Main Safeguards
docs.text:
• Use orientation only for locality; use image residuals for conformational affinity.
  • Normalize overlapping patch weights so particles are not double counted.
  • Keep feature extraction fixed during the first AP implementation.
  • Represent a global state with all its view-specific exemplars.
  • Bound dense AP memory before allocation.
  • Export results before allowing destructive project updates.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
The method is cluster tracking with a global 3D anchor:

  1. overlapping angular patches supply local diffusion features;
  2. local AP selects particle exemplars using joint 2D/3D distance;
  3. global AP groups those exemplars into conformational states;
  4. the flex_analysis basis maps each state into 3D;
  5. particle reconstructions validate the maps.

Particles may appear in several angular analyses, but each particle has one orientation, one final conformational state, and one contribution to each reconstruction.

docs.title: Standalone Cartesian pose refinement in refine3D
docs.text:
Superseded (2026-10-01). The code this note describes (refine=pose_cont, pose_cont_route, simple_pose_cont_refine3D_adapter, simple_cartesian_pose_refiner, simple_strategy3D_pose_cont, simple_pose_cont_run_stats, the program refine3D_pose_cont) was replaced by the pose_cont refactoring (doc/refactoring_notes/completed/pose_cont_refactoring.md): refine=cont, the cftc classes cartft_calc and cartft_pose_opt, strategy3D_cont, and the polish as a scheduled pass (pose_cont=yes). The current policy is in doc/policies/3D/refine3D_policy.md ("Continuous Cartesian pose policy") and refine3D_auto_policy.md (section 7). This note is kept as the record of the earlier design and its validation.

Contract status: IMPLEMENTED; matcher consolidation and the compact matched- projector regression passed compilation and runtime validation.

This living note keeps two deliberately separate routes:

  • pose_cont=yes preserves the post-matcher transaction introduced by commit 65624b924; it polishes the authoritative PFTC or inpl_cont winner.
  • refine=pose_cont selects the bona fide standalone local-search strategy. It starts from initialized ptcl3D poses and owns particle-pose search without executing PFTC or inpl_cont.

The selectors are mutually exclusive. The standalone implementation is feature-complete. The three final source-review findings are corrected, and the affected compact and Server validation has passed.

docs.title: Scientific contract
docs.text:
1. strategy3D_pose_cont is a bona fide strategy class in simple_strategy3D_pose_cont.f90 and implements the standard strategy3D lifecycle: new, srch, oris_assign, and kill.
  2. The strategy is a local continuous polisher, not an ab-initio orientation finder. Every active particle must have a positive state, a valid half-set, finite Euler angles and shifts, and a positive stored projection index. Identity Euler angles are valid.
  3. refine3D owns the common plumbing: reference masking, filtering and centering; raw particle reads; noise normalization and masking; Fourier cropping; CTF metadata; shell-noise weights; half-set identity; and reconstruction.
  4. One immutable pose_cont_reference_workspace is shared by a matcher pass. Each strategy instance binds that workspace, one thread-local Cartesian image, and its batch-local particle index.
  5. Search ownership is Cartesian only. The standalone strategy does not initialize or call strategy3D_srch, PFTC projection banks, PFTC scoring, discrete in-plane search, or inpl_cont.
  6. State and half-set are fixed. The selected LM route refines the stored rotation and shift within its local bounds.
  7. An accepted improvement is converted to SIMPLE Euler angles and native-pixel shifts. Invalid, bounded-out, or non-improving transactions preserve the seed. The Cartesian objective never replaces the PFTC corr.
  8. Reconstruction remains unchanged and consumes the resulting project pose.
  9. The production Cartesian LM objective is normalized correlation (POSE_CONT_OBJECTIVE_CART_NCC). Cartesian Euclidean remains an internal validation option. SIMPLE's surrounding objfun=euclid|cc contract is independent and does not select the Cartesian objective.

docs.title: Implemented ownership map
docs.text:
• simple_ui_refine3D.f90 exposes the standalone refine=pose_cont choice and documents its separation from pose_cont=yes.
  • simple_matcher_refvol_utils.f90 reuses ordinary reference preparation but skips PFTC bank generation for the Cartesian-only route.
  • simple_matcher_ptcl_batch.f90 reuses ordinary particle I/O while skipping polarization and unused padded per-thread images.
  • simple_strategy3D_matcher.f90 validates seeds, routes the standalone class, binds matcher-owned context, and preserves ordinary reconstruction.
  • simple_strategy3D_pose_cont.f90 owns the standalone strategy lifecycle and project-pose transaction.
  • simple_pose_cont_refine3D_adapter.f90 owns reference workspaces, particle preparation, route selection, rollback, and Cartesian sigma contributions.
  • simple_cartesian_pose_refiner.f90 remains the numerical owner of the two-parameter shift and five-parameter Cartesian LM solves.
  • simple_euclid_sigma2.f90 accepts per-particle Cartesian residual-shell contributions without requiring a PFTC object.

docs.title: new
docs.text:
• Retain particle identity and validate the standalone strategy contract.
  • Require oritype=ptcl3D, objfun=euclid, and inpl_cont=no.
  • Do not initialize inherited PFTC search state.

docs.title: bind_context
docs.text:
• Bind the matcher-owned reference workspace and builder/parameter context.
  • Bind a thread-local cropped image and record the batch-local particle index.
  • Copy the matcher-owned LM route and bounds so execution and reporting use the same canonical adapter policy.

docs.title: srch
docs.text:
1. Capture the stored pose as both seed and rollback point.
  2. Prepare the already-loaded particle on the Cartesian Fourier grid.
  3. Select shell weights and the matching state/half reference.
  4. Run shift_then_joint or joint LM from the stored pose.
  5. Stage an accepted pose; otherwise retain the seed.
  6. Evaluate the terminal pose for sigma accounting and assign the result.

docs.title: oris_assign
docs.text:
• Commit Euler angles and native-pixel shifts only after accepted improvement.
  • Preserve corr, state, half-set, and discrete seed fields.
  • Refresh convergence telemetry from the actual seed-to-terminal motion; do not retain values from the project that supplied the initial pose.

docs.title: kill
docs.text:
• Release local orientation state and nullify borrowed pointers.
  • Do not destroy matcher-owned images, builder state, or reference workspaces.

docs.title: Completed pre-commit corrections
docs.text:
1. Compile blocker: removed the accidental leading n before the result%bound_hits assignment in add_stage_accounting.
  2. Preserve the delivered post-PFTC contract: pose_cont=yes supports ordinary and probabilistic pose-search modes only after a valid assignment. It rejects sigma, eval, and fixed-orientation prob_state modes rather than polishing a stale or intentionally fixed seed.
  3. Make standalone convergence metadata authoritative: strategy3D_pose_cont now refreshes dist, dist_inpl, shincarg, mi_proj, mi_state, and the local-search frac policy for every terminal transaction, including rollback. The matcher writes frac_greedy=0 for the standalone route. The earlier Server output inherited stale values from the input project, so its convergence declaration and search-statistics lines remain non-acceptance evidence until the smoke test is repeated.

The compact class test currently proves the identity-seed validation contract; the complete class lifecycle is covered only by the production smoke run. A focused lifecycle test remains desirable but is not required to diagnose the three corrections above.

docs.title: Observed Server evidence
docs.text:
Evidence directory: pose_cont_strategy_20260916_125215.

  • The compact numerical and adapter suites passed.
  • Standalone refine=pose_cont processed all 3,081 particles, reconstructed normally, and ended with SIMPLE_REFINE3D NORMAL STOP. Matcher time was 595.59 seconds and peak RSS was 2.532 GiB.
  • The retained refine=shc pose_cont=yes route and the default refine=shc pose_cont=no route also ended normally.

These three runs are functional smoke evidence, not a matched scientific or performance comparison. The standalone run reported starting-reference foreground sigma near 1.14e-2, while both SHC runs reported about 1.32e-2. The standalone and post-PFTC runs reused canonical sigma state, whereas the default SHC run rebuilt it. Therefore their FSC and runtime differences cannot be attributed solely to the selected search route.

The post-PFTC handoff investigation found that PFTC preparation mutates its particle image. The adapter now preserves the raw particle before PFTC and owns the copy through Cartesian preparation. Matched production runs reproduced the cropped and padded preparation boundaries exactly, and the adapter contract tests cover Euler/matrix conversion, native/cropped shifts, accepted assignment, rollback, and metadata preservation.

Final corrected evidence directory: pose_cont_strategy_20260916_150959.

  • Both compact suites passed: numerical owner, solver, complete numerical suite, and refine3D adapter.
  • Standalone refine=pose_cont processed all 3,081 particles, rebuilt the canonical sigma state, reconstructed normally, and ended with SIMPLE_REFINE3D NORMAL STOP.
  • Corrected telemetry reports zero greedy searches, 100% local-search coverage, 2.855 degrees mean seed-to-terminal orientation motion, 2.374 degrees mean in-plane motion, and 0.396 pixels mean shift motion. The run is correctly not declared converged after this one iteration.
  • Matching took 747.38 seconds, peak matcher RSS was 2.682 GiB, and the final FSC resolutions were 3.617 A at 0.143 and 4.322 A at 0.5.

docs.title: Matcher consolidation and compact boundary regression
docs.text:
The final cleanup keeps simple_strategy3D_matcher orchestration-only:

  1. simple_pose_cont_refine3D_adapter constructs the canonical route policy and native-to-cropped shift limits for both pose-cont entry routes.
  2. The adapter validates global sigma-shell and particle bounds, constructs the zero-based particle sigma vector, and prepares the Cartesian particle data. A compact pose_cont_particle_spec groups state, half-set, particle index, shell range, and CTF metadata; the large particle and sigma arrays remain borrowed inputs. The matcher and standalone strategy no longer duplicate this numerical plumbing.
  3. The compact numerical suite compares the Cartesian gather with SIMPLE's established oversampled projector kernel at identical rotated coordinates from the same physical reference. Correlation, fitted gain, and relative-L2 gates protect the matched reference boundary without production diagnostics.

Compilation and both compact suites passed on 2026-09-21. The matched-projector regression reported correlation 1.0000E+00, fitted gain 1.0000E+00, and relative L2 1.4300E-07; the numerical, solver, mother, and adapter suites all reported PASS.

docs.title: Remaining validation and delivery order
docs.text:
1. Run current-master one-iteration smokes for default-off, post-matcher pose_cont=yes, standalone refine=pose_cont, and probabilistic polishing.
  2. Design the separate developer refine3D_auto_pose_cont policy, including standalone particle sampling, without changing the established refine3D_auto UI.
  3. Validate the final objective and acceptance policy on a harder real dataset.

docs.text:

docs.title: How to test the completed numerical package
docs.text:
Build SIMPLE through the normal Linux workflow, place the resulting build/bin and build/scripts directories on PATH, and run the single authoritative entry point from the stable project parent:

cd "$HOME/Projects"
bash "$HOME/Projects/hael_SIMPLE-rsync-test/production/tests/pose_cont_validation/run_oracle_validation.sh"

The runner created one timestamped continuous_3D_pose_validation_* directory directly below ~/Projects, continued through independent cases after an individual failure, and wrote the aggregate result to STATUS.txt and analysis/summary.json. The validation package and its README were removed with the retired implementation; the recorded results below are the surviving evidence.

The latest authoritative handoff rerun is ~/Projects/continuous_3D_pose_validation_20260831_121306. Passing this package establishes the numerical and regression contracts in this record. It does not activate pose_cont, add a refine3D caller, or establish real-data utility.

docs.title: Request and context
docs.text:
Hans requested implementation validation before production policy. The existing research code supplies a local five-parameter analytic Jacobian and Levenberg--Marquardt (LM) solve in a Cartesian Fourier-plane workspace. It has passed componentwise finite differences and matched-model capture experiments, but its complete weighted objective, normal equations, LM proposal, and independent forward model have not yet been verified by structurally separate oracles.

Hans also clarified the ownership boundary: particle-pose refinement must not be implemented as a callable feature of reconstructor_pcg. It requires its own particle-pose numerical module. Operations proven independent of reconstruction state may move to a neutral shared module used by reconstruction and pose refinement.

The feature must not be called PCG pose polishing. PCG solves for a 3-D volume at fixed particle poses. The five-parameter LM solves for one particle pose against a fixed volume.

docs.title: Baseline and problem
docs.text:
• reconstructor_pcg provisionally contains the Cartesian forward-plane, CTF/sigma, pose-normal-term, and bounded LM routines used by the research tests.
  • Focused tests cover fast Kaiser--Bessel derivatives, normalized stencils, shift and rotation derivatives, exact-pose stationarity, capture range, route dependence, bounds, and terminal states.
  • The principal capture observations were generated by the same forward evaluator used by the optimizer, so they do not provide an independent forward-model test.
  • No normal refine3D workflow calls the five-parameter LM, and ordinary SIMPLE behavior is unchanged.

Substantial risk remains in shell weighting, CTF application, $J^HJ$, $J^Hr$, damping and scaling, the dense five-by-five solve, rollback, shared forward-model assumptions, and numerical ownership. Production integration is premature until these contracts are independently verified and particle-pose code no longer depends on a volume-reconstruction object.

docs.title: Required outcome
docs.text:
Separate particle-pose numerics from the PCG volume solver without intentionally changing the mathematics, then independently validate the Cartesian five-parameter evaluator and LM driver over representative CTF, shell-variance, volume, box, and frequency configurations. The completed work provides numerical evidence and a handoff only; it adds no production caller.

Completion requires:

  1. independent agreement for the weighted objective, gradient, Gauss--Newton matrix, and one damped LM proposal under tolerances frozen before formal acceptance;
  2. explicit finite behavior for valid CTF/sigma configurations and an explicit nonfatal outcome for unusable variance inputs;
  3. separately declared contracts for analytic Fourier objects, tiny-box brute-force DFT, slow Cartesian interpolation, and finite-box projection;
  4. complete pose restoration after every rejected outcome;
  5. consistent results across multiple boxes, Fourier ranges, and asymmetric volumes;
  6. a particle-pose module independent of reconstructor_pcg, with only proven state-independent operations in a neutral shared module;
  7. focused pose and ordinary reconstruction regression evidence on Oracle Linux; and
  8. no UI, production caller, persistence, distributed workflow, or automatic activation.

Passing this endpoint permits a separate future development record for a standalone continuous refine3D validation mode. It does not authorize that caller or normal refinement integration.

docs.title: Pose, prepared reference, and weighted objective
docs.text:
For an input pose $(R_0,t_0)$,

$$ q=(\omega_x,\omega_y,\omega_z,t_x,t_y), \qquad R=R_0\exp([\omega]_\times). $$

Rotations are right tangent-space increments in radians and shifts are image-plane pixels of the reference box. A pose-reference constructor accepts the physical volume $X$, applies the inverse Kaiser--Bessel envelope internally,

$$ X_{\mathrm{prep}}=E^{-1}X, $$

and retains one immutable Cartesian Fourier reference until the physical volume changes. Callers do not pass an ambiguously pre-corrected volume.

For detector frequency $(h,k)$, define

$$ S(h,k;t)=\exp\left[i\frac{2\pi}{N}(ht_x+kt_y)\right], \qquad T_{\mathrm{pose}}(h,k)=\frac{C(h,k)}{\sqrt{\sigma^2_{s(h,k)}}}. $$

$T_{\mathrm{pose}}$ contains the CTF and noise amplitude only; it never contains a shift phase. The pose evaluator alone applies $S(t)$, so a shift cannot be counted twice. The whitened prediction, observation, residual, and objective are

$$ \widehat Y_w=S(t)T_{\mathrm{pose}}G_R(X_{\mathrm{prep}}), \qquad Y_w=\frac{Y}{\sqrt{\sigma^2_s}}, \qquad r=\widehat Y_w-Y_w, \qquad \Phi(q)=\frac12\sum_{(h,k)\in\Omega}|r(h,k)|^2. $$

The CTF is applied to the prediction, not divided out of the observation. CTFFLAG_NO gives $C=1$, the normal mode uses the signed CTF, and CTFFLAG_FLIP uses $|C|$. A physical CTF zero is valid. This is not the PFTC matcher objective and requires no polar-coordinate radial/Jacobian scaling factor.

docs.title: Executed forward-model conventions
docs.text:
• $N$ is even. The spatial origin is zero-based $j=N/2$, or one-based Fortran $i=N/2+1$.
  • $(h,k)$ are native integer Fourier coordinates. The gather samples the padded lattice at $\mathrm{padf}[h,k,0]R$.
  • The forward transform uses the negative exponential. The padded FFT contributes $1/N_{\mathrm{pd}}^3$ and the gather contributes $\mathrm{padf}^3$, giving native normalization $1/N^3$.
  • The rotation update is right-sided. For Cartesian unit axis $e_a$, $\partial\operatorname{loc}/\partial\omega_a=\operatorname{loc}\times e_a$.
  • The positive shift phase above gives $\partial M/\partial t_x=i(2\pi h/N)M$ and $\partial M/\partial t_y=i(2\pi k/N)M$.
  • The active domain is the full redundant Fourier disk

$$ \Omega=\left{(h,k)\in[-N/2,N/2]^2: k_{\min}^2\le h^2+k^2\le k_{\max,\mathrm{effective}}^2\right}. $$

Conjugate mates and logical positive and negative Nyquist endpoints remain explicitly counted. Validation, the later standalone mode, and the first complete refine3D integration retain this representation and log fourier_domain=full_redundant_disk, requested and effective shell limits, and active sample count. A weighted half-plane requires a separate post-integration review, conjugate/DC/Nyquist weighting, equivalence tests, and real-dataset A/B evidence.

The variance input contains one noise-power value per shell, with $s(h,k)=\operatorname{nint}\sqrt{h^2+k^2}$, and the pose path sets

$$ k_{\max,\mathrm{effective}}= \min\left(k_{\max,\mathrm{requested}},\operatorname{ubound}(\sigma^2),N/2\right). $$

Every used variance must be positive and finite. No usable shell overlap or an invalid used value returns a nonfatal invalid-noise-range outcome without changing the pose or stopping SIMPLE. The pose path does not extend the final variance into unknown shells. The existing PCG helper retains its last-shell fallback unchanged; implementation comments and diagnostics must make the difference visible for later dataset testing.

The fast normalized Kaiser--Bessel derivative holds $i_0=\operatorname{nint}(\operatorname{loc})-\mathrm{iwinsz}$ fixed. Half-integer stencil boundaries are non-differentiable, and switches are measured separately rather than included in centered finite-difference acceptance.

docs.title: Local derivatives and LM
docs.text:
The five residual-Jacobian columns differentiate the executed fast Kaiser--Bessel polynomial and normalized stencil inside one fixed interpolation cell. The LM step is

$$ (J^H J+\mu D)\delta=-J^H r. $$

Independent evidence covers the unscaled and scaled normal terms, damping diagonal, proposed step, predicted reduction, recomputed objective, gain ratio, decision, and rollback.

docs.title: Tolerance-calibration protocol
docs.text:
Use separate algebraic, LM, derivative, and forward-model tolerance families. Existing finite-difference tolerances do not qualify as algebraic or forward-model tolerances. Scalar, vector, matrix, and complex comparisons use the componentwise combined rule

$$ |a-b|\le\tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\max(|a|,|b|). $$

For complex values, $|\cdot|$ is complex magnitude. Relative comparison applies to every gradient component as well as values, residuals, and normal terms.

The original calibration fixtures use boxes $8^3$ and $12^3$. The observed box-$10^3$ and box-$16^3$ forward-hierarchy cases are retained as diagnostic regressions, not reused as untouched acceptance evidence after the 2026-08-28 amendment. The amended forward calibration must predeclare fresh holdout boxes, volumes, and rotations before execution. Calibration and holdout sets use different deterministic asymmetric volumes and poses and cover the complete declared sampling domain for their tolerance family. Before calibration, each family records its absolute floor, relative floor, and relative-scale floor. Calibration records maximum absolute and scaled-relative errors and sets

$$ \mathrm{atol}=8E_{\mathrm{abs,max}}, \qquad \mathrm{rtol}=8E_{\mathrm{rel,max}}, $$

subject to the predeclared floors. A scientifically loose result stops for diagnosis rather than becoming an acceptance threshold.

For the scaled LM system $Az=b$, compare every solution component, the physical step after coordinate rescaling, predicted and actual reductions, gain ratio, and backward error

$$ \eta=\frac{\lVert Az-b\rVert_\infty} {\lVert A\rVert_\infty\lVert z\rVert_\infty+\lVert b\rVert_\infty}. $$

Tight step agreement applies only to reliable systems; singular or poorly conditioned fixtures verify their terminal outcome instead. Ordinary decision fixtures remain away from the LM ratio threshold: for the current $0.25$ threshold, use ratios below approximately $0.20$ or above $0.30$ and test the boundary separately.

Terminal status, sample counts, active masks, invalid-input classification, symmetry, and zero contracts remain exact. Rejected-trial rollback is bitwise identical where the representation permits it. The evidence package records fixtures, raw error tables, derived tolerances, safety factor, source commit, compiler, precision, and a pre-acceptance freeze marker. A failed acceptance test reopens the protocol or implementation; it never changes a threshold in place.

docs.title: Approved forward-model amendment — 2026-08-28
docs.text:
Only the executed_dft, slow_gather, and finite_projection tolerance families are reopened. The algebraic, LM-system, derivative, and analytic-DFT families remain frozen. The amended calibration must sample multiple predeclared arbitrary rotations over every point in the full redundant Fourier disk at the calibration boxes, retain structurally separate direct-DFT and slow-gather paths, and report stencil-switch counts separately.

The arbitrary-rotation finite-box comparison is split into two contracts. The acceptance contract compares the normalized two-dimensional DFT of a line-sum projection of a rotated/resampled finite volume $X_R$ with the three-dimensional DFT of that same $X_R$ at $l=0$. A separate diagnostic compares $X_R$ with the original physical volume evaluated at rotated frequencies and reports clipping fraction, real-space interpolation error, and support margin without requiring machine agreement.

The expanded calibration derives and freezes new values for the three reopened families before any fresh holdout case runs. The already observed box-$10^3$ and box-$16^3$ results cannot set a tolerance and remain diagnostic evidence. Candidate fresh holdout boxes $14^3$ and $18^3$ require a static indexing and runtime-cost check before they are declared and frozen.

docs.title: Numerical ownership
docs.text:
The dependency direction is

$$ \text{pose refinement}\longrightarrow\text{neutral Cartesian/KB utilities} \longleftarrow\text{PCG reconstruction}. $$

The pose owner never imports simple_reconstructor_pcg, and the reconstruction owner never imports the pose owner. A later refine3D strategy may orchestrate the pose owner, but no strategy owns its numerical objective or LM implementation.

docs.title: Particle-pose owner
docs.text:
Create src/main/volume/simple_cartesian_pose_refiner.f90 with module simple_cartesian_pose_refiner. The file is under volume because it owns an immutable padded Fourier representation of a fixed physical volume and therefore depends on image/FFT infrastructure; logically, its unknown is still one particle pose, not a volume. It is not a reconstructor, a PCG component, or a workflow strategy.

The module owns:

  • the cartesian_pose_refiner lifecycle and its private immutable Fourier-reference state;
  • construction from one physical real-space volume, including the contractually required inverse-envelope preparation, centered padding, FFT, packed-lattice snapshot, wrap metadata, and full-disk bounds;
  • the pose-specific effective shell range and invalid-noise-range outcome;
  • pose transfer and observation preparation, with build_pose_transfer accepting CTF and variance but no shift argument;
  • right tangent-space rotation increments;
  • value/gradient sampling wrappers, shift validation primitives, the five-column residual Jacobian, fused objective, $J^Hr$, $J^HJ$, and stencil-switch telemetry;
  • the two-parameter validation LM and the five-parameter scaled LM, including masks, damping, Cholesky solve, bounds, gain ratio, terminal outcomes, traces, and rollback; and
  • pose-owned status constants and numerical floors.

The public pose API accepts a physical volume and particle data. A private-field cartesian_pose_data value is prepared once from the raw observation, CTF parameters, variance vector, and requested shell range; it contains the whitened observation, shift-free transfer, and effective range. Objective and LM calls accept this prepared value rather than an arbitrary transfer array. The API does not accept a reconstructor_pcg, pcg_fourier_workspace, PCG transfer object, PCG envelope array, solver accumulator, or reconstruction policy. The physical-volume constructor is the only normal route to a reference, so callers cannot silently omit or double-apply $E^{-1}$.

Current routines move from simple_reconstructor_pcg.f90 to this owner without intentional mathematical change:

Current routine Current line Target responsibility right_increment_rotation 312 Right-sided $SO(3)$ update begin_fourier_workspace and kill_fourier_workspace 1041, 1064 Replace with the pose-reference constructor/destructor get_fourier_workspace_lims2 and set_fourier_workspace_shell_range 1081, 1088 Pose-domain and effective-shell access sample_fourier_with_grad 1102 Pose wrapper over the neutral packed gather shift_residual, shift_jvp, shift_jhz, shift_normal_terms, and shift_objective_gradient 1125–1279 Retained validation-facing shift primitives rotation_jvp, pose_normal_terms, and pose_objective_gradient 1282–1389 Five-parameter derivative and normal terms count_stencil_switches 1393 Local-cell telemetry refine_shift_lm 1414 Retained two-parameter validation solver refine_pose_lm, apply_pose_parameter_mask, and solve_pose_cholesky 1547–1801 Five-parameter LM and dense solve

The current pcg_fourier_workspace type and pose/shift LM constants leave simple_reconstructor_pcg after all pose tests use the new owner. They are not kept as forwarding aliases because that would preserve the wrong public ownership boundary.

docs.title: Neutral numerical owners
docs.text:
Neutral interfaces contain no particle policy, LM state, reconstruction accumulators, or owner types. Their array bounds, normalization, precision, packing, periodic wrapping, and failure behavior are explicit arguments or documented return contracts.

Keep the executed kernel and envelope mathematics in their existing neutral modules:

Neutral routine File and line Decision kbinterpol%apod_fast_value_deriv src/main/interp/simple_kbinterpol.f90:181 Keep as the derivative of the executed fast polynomial kbinterpol%apod_mat_3d_fast_grad src/main/interp/simple_kbinterpol.f90:343 Keep as the normalized fixed-cell stencil derivative kb_stencil_envelope_1d src/main/interp/simple_gridding.f90:78 Keep as the common discrete KB-envelope definition kb_stencil_inv_envelope_1d and deapodize3D_inplace src/main/interp/simple_gridding.f90:109,128 Keep; add an explicit centered-crop variant for a native volume inside a padded-period envelope

The centered-crop inverse-envelope operation is defined by the padded period $N_{\mathrm{pd}}$, native box $N$, centered offset $o=(N_{\mathrm{pd}}-N)/2$, and the production KB window. It evaluates and center-normalizes the one-dimensional discrete envelope over period $N_{\mathrm{pd}}$, takes the guarded reciprocal only at padded indices $o+1:o+N$, and returns exactly $N$ native-axis factors. It must not substitute the native-period result from kb_stencil_inv_envelope_1d(N,...). The eventual procedure name and Fortran argument form are implementation decisions for Phase 2; these numerical inputs and returned indexing are contractual.

Create src/main/interp/simple_cartesian_fourier.f90 for the state-independent Cartesian-lattice operations that are currently embedded in the PCG owner:

Current routine Current line Neutral operation pad_vol and crop_vol 865, 876 Exact centered array embedding/cropping pair extract_native_plane 1993 Full redundant native-disk extraction from an FFT image gather_window 3630 Packed/Friedel Kaiser–Bessel value gather gather_window_grad 3663 Identical gather traversal for value and three fixed-cell derivatives

The neutral gather accepts the Fourier array, wrap table, stencil origin, and weights explicitly. It does not accept either owner object. PCG value gathers and pose value/gradient gathers must call these common routines. PCG scatter, folding, kernel, prior, accumulation, and solver operations are not neutral and do not move.

simple_reconstructor_pcg.f90:481 retains the reconstruction operator's three-dimensional build_env state, but its one-dimensional envelope and centered reciprocal construction use simple_gridding. The pose constructor uses the same neutral envelope definition. This shares the convention without transferring PCG deapodization policy into pose refinement.

docs.title: PCG reconstruction owner
docs.text:
src/main/volume/simple_reconstructor_pcg.f90 continues to own reconstructor_pcg, pcg_solver_outcome, operator-mode constants, particle accumulation, forward/adjoint reconstruction operators, preconditioner, kernel, priors, PCG solve, and profiling. In particular:

  • set_volume, forward_plane, fourier_dot, and adjoint_plane_add remain reconstruction-facing methods;
  • build_transfer remains unchanged because reconstruction includes the stored particle shift and retains its existing last-variance-shell fallback;
  • whiten_observation remains unchanged as a PCG-side compatibility helper for reconstruction regression tests;
  • extract_native_plane may remain as a thin reconstruction wrapper over the neutral routine so existing reconstruction strategies do not acquire a new dependency during the first extraction; and
  • simple_rec3D_pcg_strategy.f90 remains the owner of reconstruction batching and calls no pose LM.

The pose module deliberately implements a distinct build_pose_transfer and variance check because its transfer excludes shift and must cap the effective shell range rather than repeat the last known variance. These differing policies must not be hidden behind one ambiguous shared helper.

docs.title: Strategy and test ownership
docs.text:
src/main/strategies/search/simple_pcg_pose_polisher.f90 is not a valid numerical owner and has no production caller. Its disposition is:

Current content Current line Action polish_fixed_volume_shifts 52 Move batch accounting/rollback coverage to a test helper; call the pose owner per particle polish_fixed_volume_poses and refine_one_pose 131, 195 Move OpenMP batch/equivalence coverage to a test helper; keep single-particle LM in the pose owner execute_final_pcg_pose_polish 243 Delete after migration; do not translate this retired post-reconstruction workflow validate_batch_shapes and pcg_pose_polish_summary 484, 30 Move only the evidence-oriented shape/accounting logic needed by tests

The test helper is production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_batch_helpers.f90; it is not production API. Existing derivative, recovery, capture, mechanism, contract, and operator tests migrate from pcg_fourier_workspace and simple_pcg_pose_polisher to the new pose owner. Ordinary PCG tests continue to exercise reconstructor_pcg directly.

docs.title: Extraction invariants
docs.text:
The ownership change is accepted only if all of the following remain true:

  1. The new pose module contains no use simple_reconstructor_pcg and exposes no PCG-named type or argument.
  2. Neutral modules contain no pose status, LM, CTF/sigma policy, PCG accumulator, or solver state.
  3. PCG and pose gathers call the same neutral packed/Friedel traversal and executed KB routines.
  4. PCG transfer semantics and last-shell fallback remain byte-for-byte source-equivalent until separately reviewed.
  5. Pose transfer has no shift input and reports its requested/effective shell range and full-disk sample count.
  6. The retired post-reconstruction routine and its strategy module disappear once their test-only logic has moved.
  7. Current pose evidence is reproduced before new oracle acceptance, and ordinary reconstruction satisfies AC-12.

This map defines ownership only. It does not authorize implementation until the contract and later execution approach are separately approved.

docs.title: Independent forward evidence and comparison contracts
docs.text:
Independence comes from four paths: the executed fast gather, a structurally separate slow interpolator, a tiny-box brute-force DFT, and a finite-box real-space projection followed by FFT. The direct oracle uses

$$ F(\boldsymbol{\xi})=\frac{1}{N^3}\sum_{\mathbf{x}}X(\mathbf{x}) \exp\left(-2\pi i\boldsymbol{\xi}\cdot\mathbf{x}\right), \qquad \boldsymbol{\xi}_R=N^{-1}[h,k,0]R, $$

with spatial-frequency derivative

$$ \nabla_{\boldsymbol{\xi}}F(\boldsymbol{\xi}) =-\frac{2\pi i}{N^3}\sum_{\mathbf{x}}\mathbf{x}X(\mathbf{x}) \exp\left(-2\pi i\boldsymbol{\xi}\cdot\mathbf{x}\right). $$

The four comparison contracts are:

  1. Analytic object versus brute-force DFT: a tight double-precision convention test for origin, sign, frequency, and normalization.
  2. Brute-force DFT of $X$ versus executed $G(E^{-1}X)$: an interpolation-accuracy contract, not machine equality.
  3. Independent slow interpolation versus executed gather: a tighter source-fidelity contract using the same polynomial Kaiser--Bessel function, normalization, padding, packed/Friedel rules, and periodic wrapping without calling the executed gather or stencil helper.
  4. Finite-box projection versus direct DFT: a separate discrete-model contract that declares whether projection rays are summed or averaged. Line sums followed by a normalized two-dimensional FFT require an explicit $1/N$ factor to match the normalized three-dimensional DFT. Arbitrary rotations report additional clipping and real-space interpolation effects separately.

Analytic fixtures include centered and off-center deltas, separated points, and a non-collinear unequal-amplitude point set. Sampled Gaussian and sphere fixtures test robustness, not exact continuous-transform identities; a sphere cannot test rotational identifiability and a two-point object is degenerate about its connecting axis.

Preserve the existing evidence distinction. simple_continuous_3D_pcg_refinement_rotation_test.f90 remains a matched-model derivative-consistency test and is not independent evidence for CTF or whitening order. New independent CTF/whitening tests follow simple_continuous_3D_pcg_refinement_shift_test.f90: form the raw CTF-distorted observation first, whiten it separately, and never generate oracle observations with the evaluator under test.

docs.title: Scope boundaries
docs.text:
Included:

  • independent weighted-objective, $J^Hr$, $J^HJ$, and dense LM-step oracles;
  • ownership audit and extraction into a particle-pose module, with neutral sharing only where proven;
  • CTF and shell-variance validation;
  • analytic objects, tiny-box direct DFT, slow Cartesian interpolation, and finite-box comparison;
  • multiple volumes, boxes, and Fourier ranges;
  • focused tests, Oracle Linux evidence, and documentation that separates pose LM from PCG reconstruction.

Excluded:

  • refine3D UI, commander, strategy, metadata, restart, or distributed integration;
  • replacement or modification of inpl_cont;
  • PFTC pose derivatives or a PFTC five-parameter objective;
  • production acceptance, reference-refresh, frequency, pose-prior, or route-selection policy;
  • behavioral changes to ordinary reconstruction;
  • claims of FSC, real-data, workflow, or scientific benefit.

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
• AC-1 — Objective: independent scalar accumulation agrees with the fused objective for constant and nonconstant positive shell-variance profiles under the frozen metric.
  • AC-2 — Derivatives and normals: every residual-Jacobian column, $J^Hr$ component, and symmetric $J^HJ$ entry agrees componentwise.
  • AC-3 — LM proposal: accepted and rejected proposals agree with a separate dense five-by-five solve and acceptance calculation.
  • AC-4 — State restoration: rejected, invalid, singular, bounded-out, and finite-no-improvement trials preserve the complete input pose within the declared representation tolerance.
  • AC-5 — CTF and sigma: valid CTF/sigma configurations remain finite and agree with their oracles; short variance vectors cap the pose shell range; unusable variance returns the declared nonfatal outcome; the existing PCG fallback remains unchanged.
  • AC-6 — Forward hierarchy: analytic identities and each named pair of computational paths satisfy their separately frozen contracts over the full redundant disk on fresh holdout fixtures; the matched finite-box projection contract compares the same rotated/resampled finite object, while clipping, real-space interpolation, support margin, and stencil switches remain separately reported diagnostics.
  • AC-7 — Robustness: at least two boxes, two Fourier ranges, and three deterministic asymmetric volumes pass without post-result tolerance changes.
  • AC-8 — Pose regression: existing derivative, capture, pose-recovery, and contract cases pass or receive explicitly reviewed updates.
  • AC-9 — Oracle evidence: focused cases and the complete mother suite compile and pass on Oracle Linux with retained logs.
  • AC-10 — No activation: source contains no production caller or user-visible option for this numerical-validation slice.
  • AC-11 — Ownership: particle-pose tests call the dedicated pose module; that module does not import reconstructor_pcg; shared interfaces expose no owner-specific solver or particle-policy state.
  • AC-12 — Reconstruction regression: moving shared operations does not change ordinary PCG results outside its existing numerical contract.

docs.title: Constraints and review status
docs.text:
• Preserve continuous_3D_refinement_on_pcg_operator.md as the frozen original proposal.
  • Keep calibration fixtures distinct from acceptance fixtures. Freeze metric definitions and tolerances before acceptance and do not weaken them after observing failures.
  • Use the executed polynomial and interpolation path for the implementation under test while keeping independent oracles structurally separate.
  • Hard-limit brute-force DFT to declared tiny test boxes.
  • Keep source inspection, compilation, runtime evidence, and scientific validation separate. Oracle Linux supplies authoritative compilation and runtime evidence; agents do not compile unless explicitly requested.

Known challenges are single precision and accumulated complex error, hidden reconstruction-workspace dependencies, interpolation-stencil switches, accidental inverse crime, analytic-versus-sampled fixture confusion, and objective reduction without pose correctness.

Review decisions:

  • IN REVIEW — forward-only tolerance amendment: executed_dft, slow_gather, and finite_projection require expanded arbitrary-rotation, full-disk calibration and fresh holdout fixtures. All other tolerance families remain frozen.
  • IN REVIEW — finite-projection comparison: the matched finite-object acceptance contract and separate clipping/interpolation diagnostic are approved for implementation but are not frozen until the amended calibration fixtures and derived tolerances are reviewed.
  • RESOLVED — numerical ownership: the approved routine-by-routine map separates particle, reconstruction, neutral, strategy, and test ownership.
  • FINAL — unaffected contract: the required outcome, scope exclusions, numerical ownership, AC-1 through AC-5, and AC-7 through AC-12 remain frozen as of 2026-08-26. Only the forward portions of the tolerance protocol and AC-6 are reopened by the 2026-08-28 amendment.

docs.title: Contract approval boundary
docs.text:
Everything above this boundary is approval-controlled. When Contract status becomes FINAL, these sections remain unchanged during ordinary implementation. A discovery that changes the required outcome, scope, acceptance criteria, or architectural constraints returns the contract to IN REVIEW and stops requirement-changing implementation until reapproved.

Everything below this boundary is the approved execution approach and living progress record. Phase status and evidence entries may advance during implementation. Changing phase scope, ordering, or gates requires plan review; changing anything above this boundary returns the contract to IN REVIEW.

docs.title: Execution controls
docs.text:
• Implement one phase at a time. A failed or scientifically unresolved gate stops later phases.

  • Put substantive new test cases in separate child modules. Shared helpers contain only repeated fixture, assertion, oracle, or reporting code.
  • Keep production/CMakeLists.txt unchanged and off-limits. Name every test dependency with its mother suite's established simple_<test_id>_* prefix so the existing dependency glob discovers it. Status: COMPLETE

Create simple_cartesian_pose_refiner and its private fixed-reference and prepared-particle data. Move the pose/shift methods and constants listed under Particle-pose owner without intentional mathematical change. Migrate test callers and batch accounting to test-only helpers, delete simple_pcg_pose_polisher, and update generated source maps.

Retain the current keyed diagnostics, but rename new pose-owned helpers and evidence so they do not claim to be PCG algorithms. Adapt run_oracle_pose_capture.sh for the new source owner. Do not adapt the historical production A/B or truth-matrix runners into acceptance tests.

Perform the test rename as an ownership split, not as a blind replacement of PCG with pose_cont:

  • move neutral Cartesian Fourier and KB interpolation checks to a neutral Cartesian-Fourier test owner because these operations are shared by pose refinement and reconstruction;
  • retain the volume-noise, half-set, and reconstruction-comparison cases under an explicitly PCG-reconstruction test name, without the word refinement, because they test reconstruction rather than pose_cont;
  • rename production/tests/continuous_3D_pcg_pose_capture/ and its outputs to pose_cont terminology while preserving the isolated numerical experiment;
  • retire production/tests/continuous_3D_pcg_pose_validation/ after preserving its historical evidence references because its runners still invoke the removed pcg_pose_polish production option and are not valid acceptance paths for the new owner; and
  • remove the old continuous_3D_pcg_refinement executable, filename prefix, module prefix, log labels, and generated-index entries only after every retained case has a named destination and source-reference checks find no remaining caller.

The current inventory contains no orphaned Fortran test source under the old prefix: the CMake dependency glob compiles all of them, and every module is reachable directly or indirectly from the mother executable. scaffold is a retirement candidate because it now checks only test-harness seeding and assertions; fold any still-useful deterministic-fixture check into the neutral test support before deleting it. The keyed fixed-reference, forward-path, matched-window, reference-bias, operator-contract, capture-range, and mechanism cases are not in the default schedule, but they remain reachable diagnostics and must not be classified as unused merely because the mother suite does not schedule them by default.

Tests and reason: run source import/API checks, all ten mother-suite groups, componentwise derivative checks, shift and pose recovery, serial/parallel batch equivalence, capture range, mechanism routes, and operator diagnostics. These tests prove migration parity and ownership; they do not yet provide the independent acceptance evidence.

Gate: AC-8 passes as a migration regression, AC-10 and AC-11 pass, no test imports pcg_fourier_workspace for pose work, and the deleted strategy has no remaining caller or manifest entry.

production/CMakeLists.txt is a frozen boundary for this development. Phase 3 must conform to the existing simple_<test_id>_* dependency convention; neither this phase nor a later phase may add a special test-source exception.

docs.title: Phase 4 — implement and freeze calibration infrastructure
docs.text:
Status: COMPLETE

Approved forward-calibration rework — 2026-08-28:

  • Preserve the completed algebraic, LM-system, derivative, and analytic-DFT calibration records and frozen tolerances.
  • Recalibrate executed_dft, slow_gather, and finite_projection over every point in the full redundant disk for multiple predeclared arbitrary rotations at boxes $8^3$ and $12^3$, using more than one deterministic asymmetric physical volume.
  • Keep the executed gather, structurally separate slow gather, and brute-force direct DFT as distinct computational paths. Record sample counts, stencil switches, absolute errors, and scaled-relative errors for every comparison.
  • Replace the arbitrary-rotation finite-projection acceptance comparison with the matched discrete contract defined in the approved forward-model amendment: projection/2-D DFT of $X_R$ versus the 3-D DFT of that same rotated/resampled finite $X_R$ at $l=0$.
  • Retain original-volume rotated-frequency agreement, clipping fraction, interpolation error, and support margin as diagnostics rather than forcing them into the matched finite-projection tolerance.
  • Treat the observed boxes $10^3$ and $16^3$ as diagnostics. Perform a static even-box indexing, full-disk population, memory, and brute-force operation-count review before declaring fresh holdout boxes; $14^3$ and $18^3$ are candidates, not yet frozen.
  • Derive the three amended tolerances with the existing componentwise metric, predeclared floors, and safety factor. Write a new forward-amendment freeze marker before any fresh holdout test runs. A loose calibration result stops for scientific review.

Rework gate: the three reopened families have full-domain calibration records, the finite-projection acceptance paths operate on the same finite object, fresh holdout fixtures are declared but untouched, and the amended tolerances are reviewed and frozen before Phase 8 resumes.

Local rework implementation — 2026-08-28:

  • production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_helpers.f90:9 declares two calibration-volume variants and candidate holdout boxes $14^3$ and $18^3$ while preserving boxes $10^3$ and $16^3$ as observed diagnostics. build_calibration_fixture at line 90 now produces two deterministic asymmetric volumes per calibration box. The artifact writer at line 313 emits proposed rather than frozen forward tolerances and an AWAITING_SCIENTIFIC_REVIEW marker; it does not sample a fresh holdout.
  • production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_test.f90:151 evaluates executed_dft, slow_gather, and finite_projection over four predeclared rotations and every point in the full redundant disk at boxes $8^3$ and $12^3$. The finite-projection comparison at lines 194–204 now uses the same rotated/resampled finite object on both sides. Original-volume disagreement, clipping fraction, interpolation-switch margin, and stencil-switch counts remain separate diagnostics.
  • The test repeats every calibration calculation and requires bitwise-identical records and aggregate diagnostics. It writes forward_calibration.tsv, proposed_tolerances.tsv, fixture_manifest.tsv, and forward_holdout_static_review.tsv before rejecting a scientifically loose proposal, so a failed run remains diagnosable.
  • Lightweight source inspection is complete: the changed Phase 4 sources contain no conflict markers or lines longer than 132 columns. Compilation and runtime evidence are not claimed. The next gate is the focused Oracle calibration run, followed by human review and explicit freezing of the three proposed families before any candidate holdout is constructed.

First amended calibration run and correction — 2026-08-30:

  • Oracle package ~/Projects/pose_cont_revalidation_20260830_225501 completed all calibration calculations and stopped at the intended scientifically-loose gate. slow_gather reached maximum absolute error $2.5123\times10^{-8}$ and finite_projection reached $8.2444\times10^{-9}$; both contracts are strong. executed_dft reached maximum absolute error $4.0364\times10^{-4}$ under arbitrary rotation, while identity remained near $10^{-8}$. This is the expected distinction between exact-grid evaluation and interpolation, not a fast/slow gather inconsistency.
  • The rejection came from the tolerance derivation rather than the forward numerics. The implementation independently multiplied the maximum absolute error and the maximum scaled-relative error by the safety factor. For low-amplitude Fourier samples whose comparison scale was clamped to $10^{-3}$, an absolute error near $1.0665\times10^{-4}$ became a 10.66-percent relative maximum; multiplying that number by eight proposed the meaningless relative tolerance $0.85319$.
  • The corrected combined derivation keeps each predeclared relative floor $r_0$ and calculates the part of each component error not already covered by it,

$$ q_i=\max(0,e_i-r_0s_i),\qquad a=\max(a_0,8\max_iq_i),\qquad r=r_0, $$

where $e_i$ is absolute error, $s_i$ is the stored comparison scale, and $a_0$ is the absolute floor. This matches the approved acceptance inequality $e_i\le a+rs_i$ and avoids treating low-amplitude interpolation samples as a separately maximized relative-error contract. Families 1–4 retain their exact frozen tolerances. - production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_helpers.f90 now records every comparison scale and maximum combined excess, writes both to the evidence tables, and derives only the reopened forward proposals with the combined rule. production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_test.f90 requires every observation to pass that combined proposal and requires the forward relative tolerance to remain at its predeclared floor. The correction is source-checked only; Oracle must rebuild and rerun Phase 4 before scientific review.

Corrected calibration review and freeze — 2026-08-30:

  • Oracle package ~/Projects/pose_cont_revalidation_20260830_230740 completed with POSE_CONT_REFINEMENT_TOLERANCE_CALIBRATION: PASS. It reproduced the earlier raw maxima exactly and confirmed deterministic coverage under the combined rule. The package's STATUS.txt has a blank value because the interactive shell did not populate Bash's PIPESTATUS array; the executable's terminal PASS marker is present in the complete log and is the runtime result.
  • Scientific review accepts and freezes executed_dft at absolute tolerance $6.1319031142573850\times10^{-4}$ and relative tolerance $0.03$; slow_gather at $10^{-7}$ and $2\times10^{-5}$; and finite_projection at $10^{-5}$ and $0.05$. The safety factor remains eight. These thresholds cover the calibration domain without hiding the distinction between exact-grid identity evaluation and arbitrary-rotation interpolation.
  • Boxes $14^3$ and $18^3$ are frozen as the fresh Phase 8 forward holdouts after static review of their even indexing, full-disk populations of 149 and 253, and direct-DFT costs of 408,856 and 1,475,496 voxel terms per plane. They remain unsampled. Boxes $10^3$ and $16^3$ remain prior observed diagnostics and cannot become fresh acceptance evidence.
  • production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_helpers.f90 now contains the reviewed constants and emits frozen_tolerances.tsv plus FORWARD_AMENDMENT.FROZEN. production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_test.f90 requires the derived values to equal the frozen values exactly before emitting PASS. One Oracle rebuild and focused Phase 4 rerun must confirm this frozen source state before Phases 5 and 6 run.

Frozen-source Oracle confirmation — 2026-08-30:

  • ~/Projects/pose_cont_revalidation_20260830_231612/phase4 completed with exit status 0, emitted POSE_CONT_REFINEMENT_FORWARD_AMENDMENT: FROZEN and POSE_CONT_REFINEMENT_TOLERANCE_CALIBRATION: PASS, and wrote FORWARD_AMENDMENT.FROZEN plus frozen_tolerances.tsv.
  • The derived values equal the reviewed source constants exactly. The four calibration fixtures, four full-disk rotations, diagnostic boxes 10 and 16, and unsampled frozen holdouts 14 and 18 were all reported as declared. Phase 4 is complete; no holdout observation was used to set a threshold.

Prepare evidence — 2026-08-27:

  • Added the seven-family tolerance registry, predeclared absolute, relative, and relative-scale floors, safety factor 8, loose-result stops, componentwise combined real/complex metric, raw observation retention, derived-tolerance calculation, and immutable pre-acceptance marker in production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_helpers.f90:9,27,179,223,246,277.
  • Added disjoint deterministic calibration fixtures for boxes 8 and 12 and reserved acceptance fixtures for boxes 10 and 16 in production/tests/simple_pose_cont_refinement_calibration_helpers.f90:80,129. docs.title: Flex-generated 3D particle representatives for denoise_project
docs.text: Retired (2026-10-01). denoise_project, map_params_from_den, the stk_den project field, ptcl_src and the objfun_den/objfun_den_w hybrid objective were removed from the code base. This note is kept as a design record only; nothing in it is implementable against current code.

docs.title: Status and intent
docs.text:
This is a forward-looking implementation note. It does not describe behavior that is currently available through denoise_project.

The goal is to add a 3D denoising mode to denoise_project that:

  1. starts from a fixed ptcl3D registration and mean volume;
  2. uses the flex_analysis registered-residual diffusion map to estimate a particle manifold;
  3. fits a projection-aware generative 3D model over that manifold;
  4. evaluates the forward projection of that model at every particle's latent coordinate and registered orientation;
  5. writes those predictions as the one-to-one stk_den particle representatives expected by objfun_den; and
  6. preserves the raw registered stack as the source of the Bayesian/Euclidean refinement term.

This gives denoise_project two scientific modes under one durable dual-representation project contract:

  • 2D: the current class-registered, within-class diffusion-map pre-image path;
  • 3D: the proposed globally embedded, locally generative, tomographically consistent flex path.

The 3D mode is not a second refinement engine. It produces a denoised particle-representation project. refine3D and solve3D continue to own orientation search, Bayesian scoring, pose updates, and reconstruction.

docs.title: 1. Scientific model
docs.text:
Let:

  • (y_i) be the observed particle;
  • (R_i) be its fixed input ptcl3D orientation;
  • (t_i) be its fixed input in-plane shift;
  • (z_i) be its retained diffusion coordinate;
  • (\widehat V(z)) be the flex generative 3D volume model; and
  • (P_R) be the CTF-free forward projection operator.

The generated denoised representative is

d_i = P_{R_i} V_hat(z_i).

The particle is first moved into the existing flex registered frame, so the durable output project has zero stored in-plane angle and shift and retains the registered projection direction. The generated d_i is written directly in that same frame.

The existing hybrid objective then uses:

score_i(R,t)
    = (1 - objfun_den_w) * score_raw_i(R,t)
    + objfun_den_w       * clamp(CC(reference(R,t), d_i), 0, 1).

The raw term remains the observation-driven Bayesian/Euclidean term. The flex representative supplies a lower-noise, conformation-aware orientation cue. The denoised term remains a cross-correlation term; this proposal does not change its normalization or introduce a second noise model.

docs.title: 1.1 Global modal form
docs.text:
For a global modal model,

V_hat(z_i) = V_mean + sum_q z_iq B_q,

and linearity of projection gives:

d_i = P_Ri V_mean + sum_q z_iq P_Ri B_q.

This is already the algebra used by the legacy modal pre-image path when it synthesizes a small number of target volumes. It is useful as an implementation diagnostic and baseline, but it should not silently replace the current production local-linear estimator.

docs.title: 1.2 Local-linear chart form
docs.text:
The intended production generator follows the current preimage_mode=linear model. For chart (c), centered at medoid coordinate (z_c),

V_hat_c(z_i)
    = B_c,0 + sum_q=1:d (z_iq - z_cq) B_c,q.

Here:

  • B_c,0 is the local-linear intercept volume;
  • B_c,q is the fitted tangent/slope volume for diffusion coordinate q;
  • d = min(preimage_ndim, nmodes); and
  • particle i is evaluated only within an assigned or smoothly gated local chart.

The present local-linear reconstruction already solves for d+1 components, but only finalizes and writes component 1. Components 2:d+1 are destroyed. The central model refactoring is to retain or immediately forward-project all solved components before cleanup.

docs.title: 1.3 No particle-specific 3D volumes
docs.text:
The implementation must not materialize one 3D volume per particle. Projection and latent synthesis commute:

P_Ri V_hat_c(z_i)
    = P_Ri B_c,0
    + sum_q (z_iq - z_cq) P_Ri B_c,q.

For registered particles indexed on the nspace grid, the expensive work is therefore bounded by:

ncharts * (d + 1) * nspace

component projections. Particle representatives are inexpensive 2D linear combinations of cached component projections.

docs.title: 2.1 Mode selection
docs.text:
Add an explicit public selector rather than overloading graph:

denoise_mode=2d|3d

with 2d as the compatibility default.
