  • src/main/strategies/search/simple_strategy2D_utils.f90
  • src/main/strategies/search/simple_corrmat.f90
  • Matching-only setup in src/main/strategies/search/simple_strategy2D_matcher.f90 (prep_pftc4align2D) remains get_pdim_srch() by design.

docs.title: Partial Sum I/O Confirmation
docs.text:
polar_cavger_readwrite_partial_sums('write') writes arrays that are interpolation-range class sums (pfts_even/odd, ctf2_even/odd) and not raw matching buffers.

  • Writer entry point: src/main/pftc/simple_polarft_ops_io.f90 (polar_cavger_readwrite_partial_sums)
  • Payload writers: write_pft_array_local, write_ctf2_array_local
  • Header contract: [self%pftsz, self%kfromto(1), self%interpklim, self%ncls]

Upstream, these class sums are accumulated from polarized particle data via polar_cavger_update_sums over kfromto(1):interpklim.

docs.title: Strict I/O Behavior
docs.text:
• Compatibility/padding behavior for short legacy files was removed.
  • Read helpers now enforce exact header match and fail hard on mismatches.
  • Transfer helpers perform direct full-range assignment for the stored interpolation extent.

docs.title: Practical Rule for Future Changes
docs.text: When touching any code that calls memoize4polarize or memoize4polarize_oversamp: 1. If outputs feed polar_cavger_update_sums or restoration/class-sum state, use get_pdim_interp(). 2. If outputs are used only for matching/objective/FRC scoring, use get_pdim_srch(). 3. Do not widen matching kernels unless explicitly changing search policy.

docs.title: C1. Publish the particle field before file-backed assembly
docs.text:
Where. inmem_execute_iteration in src/main/strategies/parallelization/simple_refine3D_strategy.f90, the line after the main refine3D_exec call (line 760):

call refine3D_exec(params, build, cline, params%which_iter, converged, l_write_partial_recs .and. .not. l_polish)
! a Cartesian pass draws its particle sample in the matcher (no prob_align child writes it),
! and the assembly reads the sample of the iteration (trailing update fractions) from the
! project file, so the matcher's field goes to disk before the assembly
if( params%l_cart_refine .and. l_write_partial_recs ) call build%spproj%write_segment_inside(params%oritype)

What is wrong. In shared memory the matcher changes sampled, updatecnt, pose and state in build%spproj_field and writes only algndoc.simple. For a discrete pass without a polish the project file is written by inmem_finalize_iteration, after the assembly. The gridding volassemble builds its own toolbox from the project file, and determine_trailing_update_fraction (simple_commanders_rec_distr.f90:982) rereads ptcl3D and takes N, n, the realized fraction and the first-time rows from get_group_update_counts and get_state_update_fracs. It therefore sees the previous iteration's sample. Read from the source, not observed in a run:

  • with trail_rec=yes, the first iteration of a fresh run stops: inmem_initialize clears sampled and updatecnt at startit=1 and writes the project, so get_group_update_counts finds no sample and calls THROW_HARD('requires previous sampling');
  • in later iterations the trailing blend uses the previous iteration's N and n;
  • with or without trailing, refresh_state_populations counts the previous iteration's states; those counts select the NU matching low-pass in multi-state runs (update_project_nu_alignment_lowpass).

Affected: shared memory, rec_backend=gridding, volrec=yes, no polish, every discrete mode except sigma. In the probabilistic modes the prob_align child publishes the sample, but the poses and states the parent changes still reach disk late. Not affected: the distributed path (merge_algndocs writes the project before volassemble), the polish branch (it writes before and after the polish pass), and PCG assembly (assemble_refine3D_pcg reads the in-memory builder).

Change. Replace the line and the three comment lines above it with:

if( publish_before_file_assembly(params, l_write_partial_recs, l_polish) ) &
    &call build%spproj%write_segment_inside(params%oritype)

and add, beside polish_follows:

!> gridding volassemble rereads the project file, so the field of this iteration goes to disk first;
!! the polish branch publishes its own; a sigma pass writes no orientations
logical function publish_before_file_assembly( params, l_write_partial_recs, l_polish ) result( l_publish )
    type(parameters), intent(in) :: params
    logical,          intent(in) :: l_write_partial_recs, l_polish
    l_publish = l_write_partial_recs .and. .not. l_polish .and. trim(params%refine) /= 'sigma' .and. &
        &(params%l_cart_refine .or. trim(params%rec_backend) == 'gridding')
end function publish_before_file_assembly
  • The l_cart_refine term keeps today's write for Cartesian passes on PCG. It is redundant there, since PCG assembly uses the in-memory builder, but removing it is a separate change.
  • The sigma exclusion matches the matcher (ctrl%do_write_oris is false in sigma mode) and inmem_finalize_iteration.
  • Leave both writes in the polish branch (lines 765 and 778). Do not move a bare if( l_write_partial_recs ) write above the polish branch: it would duplicate the pre-polish write.

Done when T1 passes and the fractional-update policy states the invariant (D1).

docs.title: C4. Convergence rule for refine=cont
docs.text:
Before. check_conv3D never declared convergence for a pure refine=cont pass, so the run went to maxits. A polish iteration (pose_cont=yes) uses the discrete pass's rule and is not part of this change.

Rule. A refine=cont run has converged when most particles moved by at most half a degree and at most 1 A between consecutive poses. Made exact:

  • Particle. A particle of this pass's sample (sampled at its maximum, state > 0) is stable when all three hold:
  • its transaction ended CARTFT_ACCEPTED or CARTFT_NO_IMPROVEMENT;
  • dist + dist_inpl <= 0.5 degrees;
  • shincarg * smpd <= 1 A.
  • Iteration. The iteration passes when at least 90% of the sampled particles of every populated state are stable.
  • Run. The run converges when consecutive passing iterations have together sampled at least 90% of the active particles: every active particle with sampled >= g0, where g0 is the sample generation at which the streak began. Under full sampling one passing iteration is enough. A failing iteration resets the streak. minits still applies, and the rule never extends maxits or the refine3D_auto update budget.

Notes on the rule:

  • Rotation measure. dist + dist_inpl (projection-direction plus in-plane angle, both symmetry-aware from sym_dists) bounds the rotation angle from above for small angles. The rule is therefore conservative and needs no new rotation field.
  • Shift measure. shincarg is the shift change in native pixels, so the 1 A bound converts through params%smpd, not smpd_crop.
  • Why the status is needed. A rejected transaction keeps the seed pose, so invalid preparation, an unreliable update, bound rejection, invalid numerics and the iteration limit all show zero motion. Without the status, a pass that failed on most particles would look converged. Counting those outcomes as unstable also caps failures at 10%.
  • Why per state. States do not change under refine=cont, but a small state could hide behind a large one in a global fraction.
  • For comparison. 0.5 degrees moves a point at a 100 A radius by 0.87 A; the two bounds are matched for a particle of about 230 A diameter.

Code (as implemented).

  1. Typed outcome per particle. Name the spare slot 42 pose_cont_status:
  2. in src/defs/simple_defs_ori.f90, add I_POSE_CONT_STATUS = 42, a branch in get_oriparam_ind and get_oriparam_flag, drop I_SPARE_ORIPARAM42, and leave only slots above I_LAST_NAMED_ORIPARAM in oriparam_is_spare;
  3. in src/main/ori/simple_ori.f90:1059-1060 and :1081-1082, print slots 1..I_LAST_NAMED_ORIPARAM;
  4. in src/main/project/simple_binoris_tester.f90:195, slot 42 is now named.

The record width does not change and projects written earlier read 0 there (CARTFT_NOT_ATTEMPTED). The distributed path merges the slot with the rest of the record. 2. Write it. In oris_assign_cont (simple_strategy3D_cont.f90), set pose_cont_status = real(self%status) for every searched particle, in pure and polish passes alike. 3. Decide. - Constants in simple_defs_conv.f90: CONT_CONV_ROT_DEG = 0.5, CONT_CONV_SHIFT_A = 1.0, CONT_CONV_FRAC = 0.9. - In simple_convergence.f90: the elemental cont_particle_stable(status, rot_deg, shift_a) (public, for the tester), the component cont_streak_g0 (0 when no streak runs), and the method check_cont_conv, called from check_conv3D under l_cart_refine in place of the interim block. - It logs the stable percentage per state (multi-state), of the least stable state, and the streak coverage. It writes CONT_STABLE_PCT and CONT_STREAK_COVERAGE_PCT to the stats file, and get returns both.

The shared and distributed strategies both call check_conv3D on the merged field, so the rule is the same. The distributed strategy keeps its existing extra condition iter >= startit + 2; the shared one has none. 4. Tests. - simple_convergence_tester.f90 (N25): test_cont_particle_stable (inclusive bounds, every CARTFT_* outcome) and test_cont_rule_full_sample, on a 10-particle fixture: - all stable and 9 of 10 converge, 8 of 10 do not; - all no-improvement at zero motion converges, all bound-rejected does not; - 3 px fails at smpd 1 and passes at 0.3; - a state at 60% vetoes; - minits holds. - test_cont_rule_streak: half samples complete the streak in two passing iterations, and a failing iteration resets it. - test_cartesian_pass_never_converges became test_cartesian_pass_statistics. A field without a status does not converge, and the discrete and polish checks are unchanged. - simple_strategy3D_cont_tester: the accepted solve records CARTFT_ACCEPTED, the rejected one a rejection code. - simple_binoris_tester: slot 42 is named and round-trips. 5. N20 stage e. With maxits on the command line, refine3D_auto sets minits = maxits, so e_ran_to_maxits still holds. The stage now reports e_cont_stable_pct from the stats file. 6. Policy. The rule replaces the interim text in refine3D_policy.md. Section 7 of refine3D_auto_policy.md states that an automatic maxits can stop before the update budget.

Calibration. The bounds are absolute and stated in physical units, so nothing has to be fitted before landing. Read the logged stable fraction per iteration in N20 and in a beta-gal pose_cont=only run. If runs stop early with visibly worse FSC, raise CONT_CONV_FRAC before changing the bounds.

docs.title: T1. Trailing counts of a shared-memory fractional run
docs.text:
Owner. N20 stage f, run_refine3D_discrete in src/main/commanders/test/simple_commanders_test_highlevel_cont.f90. It already runs the affected path: shared memory, gridding, refine=neigh, update_frac=0.3, two iterations, with pose_cont=no and pose_cont=yes. No new CTest entry.

Change.

  1. Set trail_rec=yes in run_refine3D_discrete.
  2. After each of the two runs, still in the stage directory (before simple_chdir(gate_root)), read refine3D_trail_manifest_fname(1) with trail_chain_manifest%read, and take nrep from the final project with out%os_ptcl3D%get_group_update_counts('state', 1, nrep, nsmp).
  3. Check nint(manifest%get_mrep()) == nrep(1) through the existing gate%check, named f_<tag>_trailing_counts_from_current_sample.

Why this is exact: with ufrac_trec unset the applied fraction equals the realized one, and population_blend_weights then returns mnew = N (simple_oris_sampling.f90:81-102). The manifest of the last assembly must therefore carry the N of the final project. Iteration 2 of a 0.3 sample has a larger N than iteration 1, so a stale count differs.

On the current ordering the pose_cont=no run stops at the first assembly (C1, first consequence), and the pose_cont=yes run passes. After C1 both pass.

docs.title: Continuous Cartesian pose refinement (refine=cont): refactoring plan
docs.text:
• Status: completed by the delegated run (section 14.1), Phases 0 to 10 done (section 15), awaiting the maintainer's review of the raw diff; O4-O8 taken as recorded under "Delegation", each open to reversal at review; doc/code_overview/fortran-indexes to be regenerated by the maintainer (Phase 10 row)
  • Scope: five-parameter Cartesian pose refinement and its integration in refine3D and refine3D_auto
  • Source baseline: the inventory was taken at master 712b4d86 and still holds at 30d23bc62 (line counts, the matcher line numbers of section 8.1 and the parameter lines cited in Phase 1 are unchanged). Phase 0 records its numbers at the commit the refactoring branches from, not at 712b4d86 (Phase 0)
  • Last updated: 2026-10-01

This document is self-contained. It holds the contract, the current-state inventory, the target architecture, the phased refactoring, and the test plan. Per repository policy the maintainer compiles and runs; the delegated run of section 14.1 compiles and runs on the Dell under the maintainer's request.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Give continuous Cartesian pose refinement the same boundaries as the rest of SIMPLE:

  • refine=cont is a refinement mode of refine3D that runs with no polar object alive, and refine3D_auto accepts it;
  • the matcher references exactly one continuous-pose symbol, strategy3D_cont;
  • the numerics sit in two encapsulated classes, a calculator owned by builder and an optimizer owned by the strategy, as in the polar path;
  • both objectives follow objfun with the polar definitions, and the reference follows the polar branch;
  • a pose polish after discrete search is available as a scheduled Cartesian pass;
  • there is no separate refine3D_pose_cont program.

Two rules hold for the whole sequence. Ownership moves and scientific changes are separate commits; Phase 3 is the only phase that changes numerics. Existing tests are reused and moved with the code they test; every new behavior lands with its test in the same phase (section 10).

docs.title: 2. Current state
docs.text:
Production code (3,147 lines in eight modules):

Module Lines Holds volume/simple_cartesian_pose_refiner.f90 1,182 Cartesian reference, particle preparation, objective and gradient, shift and joint Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) interp/simple_cartesian_fourier.f90 138 Stateless embedding, extraction and KB gathers; also used by reconstructor_pcg and flex PCA strategies/search/simple_pose_cont_refine3D_adapter.f90 745 Policy records, reference and particle workspaces, reference file I/O, observation preparation, coordinate conversion, transaction control strategies/search/simple_strategy3D_pose_cont.f90 276 Standalone refine=pose_cont strategy strategies/search/simple_pose_cont_run_stats.f90 377 Per-thread accounting and per-iteration report files commanders/simple/simple_commander_refine3D_pose_cont.f90 82 Program refine3D_pose_cont, extending commander_refine3D_auto strategies/parallelization/simple_refine3D_pose_cont_workflow.f90 196 Stage sequencing for that program ui/simple/simple_ui_refine3D_pose_cont.f90 151 Its UI

Shared files touched: simple_strategy3D_matcher, simple_matcher_refvol_utils, simple_matcher_ptcl_batch, simple_refine3D_strategy, simple_strategy3D_prob, simple_euclid_sigma2, simple_parameters*, simple_ui_refine3D, simple_exec_refine3D, simple_commanders_refine3D, simple_convergence, simple_defs_ori, simple_binoris, simple_refine3D_fnames.

What is wrong with it:

  1. The matcher hosts two continuous-pose pipelines (pose_cont=yes after a discrete winner, refine=pose_cont instead of the search). 124 of its 717 lines mention continuous-pose state; it holds the only three select type downcasts in non-test strategy code and a 55-line numerical routine (section 8.1).
  2. The adapter exports eleven public types and nine free procedures and has no type named after the module. Most procedures forward to the refiner or wrap one or two image/ori calls (section 8.2).
  3. strategy3D_pose_cont cannot satisfy the strategy3D contract: the base embeds the PFTC search object s, which it never initialises, and it needs a seven-argument bind_context and a get_result that are not in the abstract interface.
  4. The objective ignores objfun: both euclid and cc runs optimize a normalized correlation on sigma-whitened data. corr is never written.
  5. Shared helpers import the adapter and take optional feature flags (cartesian_only, pose_cont_particles); euclid_sigma2 gained a second constructor and a setter that lets an outside module write sigma2_part.
  6. Parameters: four switches, string comparisons in four modules, validation keyed on a program name, cc_emit_sigma silently forced on, LM policy hard-coded in adapter type defaults.
  7. The particle record grew from 50 to 52 reals for two telemetry flags.
  8. Reporting exists three times: per-particle fields, a stats module with its own per-partition files, and system_clock timers in the particle loop.
  9. commander_refine3D_auto was given four override hooks so that a second commander could inherit from it.
  10. 28 error stop statements in the continuous-pose code (24 in the refiner, 4 in the adapter), several reachable from the OpenMP particle loop; four of them sit in pure procedures (sample_fourier_with_grad, shift_native_to_crop, shift_crop_to_native). The four in simple_cartesian_fourier (shape checks in center_embed_real3d and center_crop_real3d) belong to the shared layer and are out of scope.

What is sound and is kept: rollback to the input pose after a failed solve; explicit shift and rotation bounds anchored at the seed; explicit even/odd reference selection; the KB derivative in simple_kbinterpol; the stateless simple_cartesian_fourier layer; the numerical tests.

docs.title: 3. Contract
docs.text:
Accepted by the maintainer on 2026-09-30.

Id Ruling C1 The matcher uses one strategy object, strategy3D_cont, and no other continuous-pose symbol. C2 simple_pose_cont_refine3D_adapter is dissolved; each piece moves to its owner. C3 The feature is restructured as encapsulated classes: private components, new/kill, type-bound behavior, one type per module named after it. C4 Both objectives are supported and follow objfun, mirroring the polar implementation. C5 sigma2 is never part of a correlation calculation. A Cartesian cc pass neither reads, requires nor writes sigma2, as in the polar branch, where sigma2 is not produced under objfun=cc (ruling 2026-09-30). The internal cc_emit_sigma of the polar CC pose initialization does not apply to Cartesian passes. C6 Cartesian euclid is the polar loss, normalized by the particle's weighted power, with exp(-L) as the stored score. C7 refine=cont is a refinement mode of refine3D, testable on its own and independent of the polar machinery. C8 Pose polishing after discrete search is supported. It is scheduled per pass: a refine=cont pass follows a discrete pass. A per-particle second stage inside one pass is not part of this plan; it can be added later on the same objects. C9 The Cartesian and polar objectives are not directly comparable. No decision compares a value from one with a value from the other. C10 The reference follows the polar branch of refine3D, including how deapodization is handled. C11 refine3D_auto supports refine=cont. In that mode it bypasses all polar machinery, including the discrete greedy initialization, and runs a purely Cartesian refinement. It is therefore a continuation mode: the project must already hold 3D poses from a discrete workflow. C12 refine=cont in refine3D_auto follows the nsample policy. C13 refine3D_pose_cont is not a separate program. C14 Each representation persists its own objective value: polar passes write corr, Cartesian passes write corr_cart. A Cartesian pass never writes corr. Stored scores are read, not recalculated by the code that needs them (ruling 2026-09-30; replaces "the refined Cartesian score is persisted in corr"). C15 The particle record carries corr_cart and the improved flag; "attempted" equals "sampled in a Cartesian pass" and needs no field. The layout is O8 (the 50-real target accepted earlier cannot hold the extra field and is superseded). C16 One LM route is kept, chosen from the Phase 0 baseline; pose_cont_route is removed and LM policy becomes private constants of the optimizer. C17 Names: folder src/main/cftc, classes cartft_calc and cartft_pose_opt, builder field cftc, and an abstract strategy3D_pftc parent for the polar strategies. New identifiers use the short form cart for Cartesian (modules, types, procedures, variables, files, suite= selectors); prose keeps "Cartesian" (2026-09-30). C18 The end-to-end gate gets its own high-level CTest entry, cont_refine3D_1jxy; SIMPLE_CTEST_BUDGET goes from 29 to 30. C19 The polish switch is pose_cont=yes\|no. When on, a Cartesian pass follows every discrete iteration, in refine3D and in refine3D_auto. C20 refine3D_auto keeps objfun=euclid; objfun=cc with refine=cont is available through refine3D only. C21 objfun_den with refine=cont is rejected in parameter validation for now. C22 The Cartesian references reach the matcher as a file of prepared real-space volumes, written once per iteration by the reference materializer and read by every matcher, shared-memory or distributed. The matcher pads and transforms them and gathers central sections on the fly; it does not prepare references itself (accepted 2026-09-30; section 6.6).

Facts verified in the source that the contract relies on:

  • C10. The polar branch prepares the reference in read_mask_filter_refvols, pads it by 2 in real space (pad_fft), expands it (expand_cmat) and gathers with normalized KB weights scaled by pf^3 (interp_fcomp_oversamp). It applies no inverse KB envelope at the gather; deapodization happens when the volume is reconstructed (reconstructor%invenv1d). The Cartesian production path (new_physical_reference) already does the same on the same prepared volume, and test_matched_projector_boundary pins its gather against interp_fcomp_oversamp. The unused new_inverse_envelope_reference is removed unless O5 is ruled (b). The polar branch also passes the particle through the same stencil (polarize_oversamp); the Cartesian particle side is O5.
  • C14. With corr_cart beside corr, the two representations never share a field: a Cartesian pass writes corr_cart for every particle it processes, accepted or not, and leaves corr as the last polar pass left it. Under pose_cont=yes, corr therefore refers to the discrete pose before the polish and corr_cart to the polished pose; under refine=cont, corr keeps the value of the discrete workflow the poses came from. Within corr, scores from different iterations and band limits still sit side by side under fractional updates, as they always have. The readers of corr, all of which now see polar values only:
  • The one routine that sorts the stored ptcl3D score is make_projdir_class_samples in refine3D_states (balance=yes with fractional updates); it orders each projection bin by corr. sample4update_class reads that order only to cut a bin to its best frac_best fraction, or to take its top nsample under greedy_sampling=yes. exec_refine3D_states sets frac_best=1.0 and greedy_sampling=no unconditionally, so the whole bin is eligible and the sample is drawn by lowest updatecnt with a shuffle: the order is never read. The final missing-update pass runs with balance=no.
  • The class-biased sampling of abinitio3D, classify3D_refs, sample_classes and bootstrap_cavgs ranks ptcl2D scores, which a Cartesian pass does not write.
  • The even/odd choice in abinitio3D_cavgs compares two polar scores of one run. gen_ptcl_mask (with frac_best), extremal_bound and get_proj_sample_stats rank corr but have no production caller.
  • Every other reader is a report (convergence statistics, the class document of cavger_gen2Dclassdoc, the abinitio3D_addon report) or tests corr against zero (has_been_searched).

The reader of corr_cart is the per-iteration report of a Cartesian pass (simple_convergence, over the particles that pass sampled). No consumer recalculates a stored score. - C15. simple_binoris%read_particle_record reads records narrower than the current width and is pinned by test_legacy_narrow_particle_records. It rejects wider ones. The record is 52 reals since 2026-09-21: slot 51 holds pose_cont_attempted, slot 52 pose_cont_improved, both 0/1, cleared by the matcher on every run, so only particles of a pose_cont run carry a 1. Slot 42 (cc_nonpeak) is unused today but carried a correlation statistic in earlier versions (its reporting was removed in e45fd1aa2, 2024-03-19), so older projects can hold values there. - C10, the reference handoff. No central section is precomputed on the Cartesian path. materialize_reprojection_model_from_volumes, in the iteration strategy, runs the reference preparation the polar branch runs (read_mask_filter_refvols: volume choice, masking, filtering, envelope; the low-resolution even/odd blend; centering, with its shift mapped into the project) and writes the prepared real-space volumes, one MRC file per state and half (pose_cont_reference_stateNN_{even,odd}.mrc). Under refine=pose_cont (cartesian_only) it skips the reprojection; under pose_cont=yes it reprojects as well. The matcher reads them (load_reference_slot), pads each by 2, Fourier transforms it once (load_pose_reference) and extracts every Fourier sample it needs at the continuous rotation by a KB gather with derivatives (sample_fourier_with_grad). What crosses the boundary is the prepared volume, not a reprojection model. The handoff stays because the preparation and the band limit are decided once, by the strategy (refine3D_policy.md, section 6), for every matcher of the iteration (section 6.6); its ownership moves (section 6.4).

docs.title: 4. Open decisions
docs.text:
Id Decision Recommendation Blocks O2 The convergence rule for refine=cont (section 7.2). Until a rule has been chosen and tested, early convergence is disabled for refine=cont: a run goes to maxits. The candidate statistics are logged every iteration so the rule can be chosen from data. Enabling an early stop; no phase

| O4 | Particle preparation (section 5, "Particle preparation" and "CTF"). The polar path centres the particle on its stored shift and phase-flips it (CTFFLAG_YES) before the soft mask; the Cartesian path masks the unshifted, unflipped particle and applies the full shift and the signed CTF to the model. The mask then cuts CTF-delocalized signal that the model still carries (at 300 kV and 1.5 um defocus the displacement lambda*df/d is 37 A at 8 A, 74 A at 4 A, 98 A at 3 A, against a 60 A mask radius in E25), and it sits off the particle centre by the stored shift. | Prepare the observation as prepimg4align does up to the mask (shift by minus the seed shift, flip for CTFFLAG_YES, soft mask at msk_crop), without the padding. The model uses abs(CTF) for CTFFLAG_YES and CTFFLAG_FLIP; the optimizer solves for the shift increment from the seed and commits seed plus increment, as assign_ori does. | Phase 3 | | O5 | Particle-side interpolation (section 5, "Particle preparation"). The polar path passes particle and reference through the same normalized KB stencil on a 2x padded grid, so both carry the same real-space taper; the Cartesian path gathers the reference that way but uses the particle on its native grid. Relative to the particle, the Cartesian reference is attenuated by the stencil's taper, per axis 0.91, 0.83 and 0.74 at 0.25, 0.35 and 0.45 box from the centre (the same within 1% off grid). It biases euclid amplitudes and makes the sigma2 of the two representations differ by the taper's noise-power factor. Options: (a) multiply the masked observation by the separable taper of the stencil before its transform, which reproduces the polar particle for on-grid samples; (b) keep the inverse-envelope reference constructor that Phase 4 deletes, which deapodizes the reference instead. | (a): it mirrors the polar branch and keeps one reference for the discrete and the Cartesian pass (C10, C22). | Phase 3; the deletion in Phase 4 | | O6 | Search bounds (section 5, "Search bounds"). The Cartesian bounds are hard-coded (5 native pixels total shift, 1 pixel per step, 15 degrees total rotation); the polar refine=neigh search is bounded by trs (shift around the stored shift) and athres (neighbourhood around the subspace peaks). | The total shift bound is trs and the total rotation bound is athres, both from parameters; C16 then covers damping, step sizes and iteration caps only. | Phase 3 |

| O7 | How refine3D_auto is switched to continuous-only refinement (C11). Today refine3D_auto hard-sets refine=prob_neigh and exposes no refine; no automated 3D workflow exposes refine. refine3D_states is the precedent: it exposes a workflow-level pose_policy, derives multivol_mode and prob_neigh_mode from it, and rejects those keys on its command line. Options: (a) expose refine=prob_neigh\|cont, as Phase 8 now says; (b) one workflow-level key for all continuous pose refinement, pose_cont=no\|yes\|only, where yes is the polish of C19 and only the continuation mode of C11. | (b). One key answers "how much continuous refinement", yes means the same in refine3D and refine3D_auto, refine stays internal, and only reads as what it is: no discrete search at all. refine3D_auto derives refine from pose_cont, rejects refine on its command line as refine3D_states rejects multivol_mode, and rejects pose_cont=only with ref_pose_init=cc or regpass=yes given explicitly. refine3D keeps refine=cont and pose_cont=yes\|no. The existing continue key (resume a previous run) is not reused. | Phase 8 | | O8 | Record layout for corr_cart and the improved flag (C15). The record is 52 reals today (slot 51 attempted, 52 improved); slot 42 is unused but holds old cc_nonpeak values in pre-2024 projects. | Keep the width at 52. Slot 51 becomes corr_cart (I_CORR_CART, flag corr_cart); slot 52 stays the improved flag with its meaning; slot 42 stays unused. No reader change is needed: 52-real projects read as they are and narrower records still read with both fields zero. The one artefact: a particle that ran the experimental pose_cont between 2026-09-21 and the cut-over shows corr_cart = 1 until its first Cartesian pass, which only a report could see, since reports read the particles the pass sampled. The alternatives each need a reader special case or reuse slot 42. | Phase 7 |

Delegation, 2026-09-30: the maintainer delegated the run and reviews the result at the end (section 14.1). The run adopts the recommendations of O4, O5 (option a), O6, O7 (option b) and O8, and the layout of section 6.6, and records each adoption in section 15 in the phase that implements it. Each remains open to reversal at the final review. O2 keeps its interim rule.

Ruling on O6, 2026-10-02 (maintainer): the total rotation bound is a parameter of its own, athres_cont, default 10 degrees, the halfwidth of the total rotation from the seed: wide enough to capture wrongly assigned orientations, and independent of athres (the polar neighbourhood radius) and prob_athres (the probabilistic threshold, which narrows to the mean angular motion). The shift bound stays trs. E25 and N20 set athres_cont 15, the Phase 0 bound.

Ruling on C16, 2026-10-02 (maintainer): production runs the joint LM stage alone (30-40 % faster on beta-gal at equal objective; refinement applies it in many rounds, so what one pass misses a later one finds). shift_then_joint stays: cartft_pose_opt%new(..., shift_first=.true.), reached from a pass through the internal parameter cont_route=joint|shift_then_joint (default joint, not in the UI). The single-pass capture gates measured on it keep it and their floors: E25 and N20 stages a-c.

O3 (ranking of stored scores of mixed origin) was withdrawn on 2026-09-30: the one ranking of stored ptcl3D scores is never read under the sampling defaults refine3D_states fixes, and C14 now keeps the Cartesian score out of corr altogether. The rescoring pass it recommended and its test (N24) are dropped.

docs.title: 5. Conventions to mirror from the polar branch
docs.text:
The reference for "mirror" is refine3D refine=neigh (strategy3D_greedy_sub), the mode refine3D_nano runs with objfun=cc for high-resolution nanoparticle refinement. Reviewed against its source on 2026-09-30. It scans a 500-direction subspace and athres neighbourhoods of its peaks on the discrete grid, searches the shift on the previous reference first (inpl_srch_first), refines shift and in-plane angle continuously on the winners, and with the default inpl_cont=yes polishes the committed assignment jointly (refine_selected_continuously). The Cartesian pass corresponds to those continuous stages, extended to the two out-of-plane angles. Verified to match, or to match once the target is implemented: the euclid measure, the cc weighting of the continuous stages, the reference and its gather, even/odd selection, the band limit, the sigma2 definition (mean squared residual over two per sample, per shell), and shift-first staging (the shift_then_joint route, which the capture experiment also found safe where rotation-first was not). Not matching: particle preparation (O4, O5), search bounds (O6) and shell membership.

Aspect Polar branch Cartesian today Target Objective selection params%cc_objfun in gen_objfun_vals Fixed in pose_cont_config (always the whitened correlation), independent of objfun Dispatch on params%cc_objfun objfun=cc Normalized correlation, no sigma2 weighting, in two weightings. The discrete scan (gen_corrs) sums rings unweighted; a ring has pftsz samples whatever its radius, so per Cartesian pixel that is a 1/k weight. The continuous stages that commit the pose and corr weight ring k by k (gen_corr_cc_for_rot_8 in the shift search, gen_normalized_corr_grad_at_angle in the inpl_cont polish), which per Cartesian pixel is uniform 1 - cc on sigma-whitened data (per-pixel weight 1/sigma2); needs sigma2, hence the forced cc_emit_sigma Uniform per pixel, no sigma2 read or required (C5): the weighting of the polar continuous stages objfun=euclid L = sum_k (k/sigma2_k) sum_p abs(X - CTF R)^2 / wsqsum(X); score exp(-L) 0.5 sum abs(r)^2 / sigma2; not normalized; no score Same loss and score (C6) Shell weight euclid: k/sigma2_k, polar Jacobian times inverse variance; cc: as above 1/sigma2 per Cartesian pixel for both euclid: 1/sigma2 per pixel, the same measure; cc: uniform. Pinned by N4, N6 Shell membership Rings at integer k, kfrom..kto Pixels with kfrom <= r <= kto, binned by nint(r): the two edge shells are half width Pixels with nint(r) in [kfrom, kto] Stored score corr holds cc or exp(-L) Not written corr_cart, written by every Cartesian pass; corr is never written by one (C14) sigma2 esig%calc_sigma2(pftc, ...) after assignment, under euclid; not produced under cc Own residual routine plus an outside setter; read and written under both objectives euclid only: the sigma owner, from the Cartesian calculator. A cc pass reads and writes none (C5) Particle preparation prepimg4align: shift by minus the stored shift, flip (CTFFLAG_YES), soft mask at msk_crop, pad by 2; polar samples by the normalized KB stencil from the padded transform, times pf^2 Noise normalization, soft mask at msk_crop with no shift and no flip, no padding; samples on the native grid; the full shift is a phase on the model O4 and O5 CTF Particle phase-flipped before the mask for CTFFLAG_YES; reference times abs(CTF) Unflipped particle, signed CTF (abs for CTFFLAG_FLIP) Equivalent only without a mask; with the mask, O4 Search bounds Shift within trs of the stored shift; directions within athres of the subspace peaks and the previous direction 5 native pixels and 15 degrees from the seed, hard-coded O6 Reference Prepared volume, pad by 2, KB gather times pf^3, no inverse envelope at the gather The same Unchanged (C10); the particle side is O5 Band limit kfromto adopted from the reprojection-model header Standalone route skips the adoption Travels in the header of the prepared reference volumes (section 6.6)

As built in Phase 3, where the target column needed a decision:

  • Shell membership: a pixel belongs to shell nint(r) and is used when that shell lies in [kfrom, kto] and the pixel lies inside the Nyquist circle, r <= box/2. The outer half of shell box/2 is beyond the band of the padded reference transform (and beyond the gather's wrap table); the polar ring of radius box/2 does not sample it either. Below the Nyquist shell the membership is exactly nint(r).
  • euclid is L = sum |X - C M|^2/sigma2 / sum |X|^2/sigma2 over that membership, the per-pixel form of the polar k/sigma2_k ring weight (a ring of the polar grid has pftsz samples at radius k; per Cartesian pixel the Jacobian k cancels); both objectives are normalized by the particle's power, so an observation without power is an invalid preparation (a per-particle status), not an undefined objective.
  • O4 is prepimg4align's fused routines in its order (norm_noise_fft_clip_shift or _ctf_flip with the shift by minus the stored shift on the cropped grid and the CTF at smpd_crop, then ifft_mask_fft, the unpadded sibling of its ifft_mask_pad_fft). The fused flip reads the memoized Fourier maps of the cropped box, so a Cartesian pass memoizes them per batch as the polar batch preparation does; the observation stops when they are absent.
  • O5 (a) is the stencil's response at period OSMPL_PAD_FAC*box, cropped to the box and unit at the centre (kb_stencil_envelope_1d), applied as taper(i)*taper(j) to the masked image before its transform. It equals the polar particle's on-grid samples of a zero-padded masked image exactly (N28). prepimg4align pads with the post-mask edge mean instead of zero; that background adds edge_mean times the aliased taper to the polar samples, which the Cartesian observation does not carry. After noise normalization the edge mean is the mean of the noise outside the mask and close to zero; the difference is recorded, not modelled.

docs.title: 6.1 Dependency direction
docs.text:
refine3D / refine3D_auto commander
    -> refine3D iteration strategy (shared-memory or distributed)
        -> matcher
            -> strategy3D_cont                       (one particle)
                -> builder%cftc   : cartft_calc (references, particles, objective)
                -> cartft_pose_opt              (LM, bounds, accept or reject)
                    -> simple_kbinterpol, simple_cartesian_fourier

The calculator and optimizer import no commander, matcher, UI, project I/O or parallelization module.

docs.title: 6.2 Classes
docs.text:
src/main/cftc/simple_cartft_calc.f90, type cartft_calc, owned by builder as cftc (the role pftc has):

  • state-by-half Cartesian references and their read/write. A reference is the prepared volume, padded by 2 and Fourier transformed once when it is read. No section is stored: the objective, gradient and prediction gather each Fourier sample at the continuous rotation, so there is no projection grid. In memory a reference is the padded transform, (2 box_crop)^3 / 2 complex values (0.54 GB per state and half at box_crop 256), held for the whole matcher pass;
  • the prepared particles of the current batch and per-thread scratch;
  • objective and gradient for cc and euclid, dispatched on cc_objfun; the cc methods take no sigma2 argument, so none can enter (C5);
  • the residual used by the sigma owner.

Built from these routines of the refiner: load_pose_reference, prepare_pose_particle, sample_fourier_with_grad, predict_unweighted_pose, shift_normal_terms, pose_normal_terms, finalize_cc_normal_terms, pose_objective_gradient, prepared_pose_sigma_contribution, pose_cont_ctf_value; and from the adapter: pose_cont_reference_workspace, load_reference_slot, write_pose_cont_reference_artifact.

src/main/cftc/simple_cartft_pose_opt.f90, type cartft_pose_opt (the role pftc_shsrch_grad has):

  • the LM solve, damping, cumulative bounds, accept or reject;
  • takes and returns ori; rotation matrices, cropped-grid shifts, normal equations and stage records are private.

Built from refine_shift_lm, refine_pose_lm, refine_prepared_pose_lm, right_increment_rotation, build_pose_lm_system, solve_pose_cholesky, increase_lm_damping, rejection_terminal_status, apply_pose_parameter_mask; and from the adapter: run_pose_cont_transaction with its helpers, the pose, config, limits and result records, and the ori conversions.

simple_cartesian_fourier stays in src/main/interp. Sources under src/main are globbed recursively, so the new folder needs only cftc.inf.

Ownership, lifetime and thread-safety:

Object Owner Lifetime Written when Read when Calculator references (state by half) builder%cftc One matcher pass read, before the particle loop, serial Particle loop, concurrently Calculator prepared particles builder%cftc One batch prepare_batch, in its own parallel loop, one particle per iteration Particle loop, concurrently Calculator work images and residual buffers builder%cftc, indexed by thread One matcher pass By the thread that owns the index By that thread only Optimizer A component of strategy3D_cont One particle: built in new, released in kill By the one thread running that particle's srch By that thread only
  • The objective, gradient and prediction methods take the calculator as intent(in), so concurrent evaluation on different particles cannot write shared state. The refiner's evaluation routines already have this form.
  • The residual method writes only the thread-indexed buffers. Today the sigma routine allocates four per-shell arrays on every call; those become the thread-indexed buffers.
  • The optimizer holds fixed-size state only (the 5x5 system, bounds, status); it allocates nothing during a solve and nothing is shared between optimizers. This mirrors strategy3D_srch owning its pftc_shsrch_grad objects.

As built in Phase 2 (review checkpoint 1; interfaces in section 15, "Phase 2 interfaces"). Calculator: new(nstates, box, nptcls), kill, set_ref(state, iseven, volume) from a prepared volume in memory (the file read/write of 6.6 call it in Phase 4), set_ptcl(iptcl, ...) per batch slot (prepare_batch fills the slots in Phase 6), and the evaluation methods predict, objective_gradient, shift_normal_terms, pose_normal_terms and sigma_contribution, all on (state, iseven, iptcl) with the calculator intent(in). The objective is an argument of the evaluation methods, OBJFUN_CC or OBJFUN_EUCLID, which in Phase 2 select the two existing objectives unchanged (the whitened NCC and the whitened half squared residual); Phase 3 gives them the definitions of section 5 and decides whether the objective becomes a property set in new. The particle record of the refiner (cartesian_pose_data) is a private type of the calculator. Optimizer: new(box, box_crop, objfun, ...) with the current policy as defaults and optional overrides (both routes through shift_first; C16 reduces them in Phase 8), refine(calc, iptcl, o) on an ori, and refine_pose on a rotation matrix and a cropped shift, which the forwarders and the 1JYX fixture need to stay bit-identical (an ori stores single precision Euler angles); the stage solvers refine_shift and refine_joint are public because E12 tests them alone; get_status, get_objectives, get_motion, get_stage read the last solve; right_increment_rotation is exported as the rotation convention the fixtures share. Phase 7 decides whether refine_pose and the stage solvers become private once the forwarders are gone. Per-particle failures are typed statuses (CARTFT_INVALID_PREPARATION, CARTFT_NO_RELIABLE_UPDATE, CARTFT_BOUND_REJECTED, CARTFT_INVALID_NUMERICS, ...); caller-contract violations are THROW_HARD; the gather is pure and returns an inside flag that its non-pure callers turn into a stop.

As built in Phase 3 (review checkpoint 2). The objective is a property of the particle slot, not of the calculator or of a call: set_ptcl is generic, set_ptcl(iptcl, observed, ctfparms, kfromto) prepares an OBJFUN_CC slot and takes no sigma2 (C5: none can enter), set_ptcl(iptcl, observed, ctfparms, sigma2, kfromto) an OBJFUN_EUCLID slot; get_ptcl_objfun reports it, and the evaluation methods lose their objective argument and dispatch on the slot. The pass chooses the preparation from params%cc_objfun, so the objective follows objfun where the particle is prepared (the batch preparation of Phase 6), and a slot cannot be evaluated under an objective it was not prepared for. The optimizer lost its objective argument with it. score(iptcl, objective) gives the stored score of the polar branch (cc, or exp(-L)), which Phase 7 writes to corr_cart; get_ptcl_taper gives the particle-side taper of O5 (a). The optimizer's new(box, box_crop, trs, athres, ...) takes the total bounds of O6 in the units of parameters (native pixels, degrees; trs = 0 freezes the shifts), and refine on an ori solves for the shift increment of an observation centred on the stored shift and commits stored shift plus increment (O4); refine_pose keeps calculator coordinates, where the shift is the model shift relative to the slot's observation.

docs.title: 6.3 Strategy hierarchy
docs.text:
strategy3D                 abstract; spec and the four deferred methods only
  strategy3D_pftc          abstract; owns s (strategy3D_srch)
    greedy, greedy_inpl, greedy_smpl, greedy_sub, shc, shc_smpl,
    snhc_smpl, eval, prob              (nine files change their parent)
  strategy3D_cont          Cartesian transaction for one particle

The matcher dereferences ptr%s in exactly two places (lines 595 and 602). Both move: the shift increment is taken from the project orientation before and after srch (s%prev_shvec is that stored shift), and the cont_inpl_* fields are written by the search object that produced them.

strategy3D_cont exposes new(params, spec, build), srch(os, ithr), oris_assign() and kill() and nothing else.

As built in Phase 5. simple_strategy3D_pftc holds the abstract strategy3D_pftc, which extends strategy3D by the one component s; the nine polar strategies extend it, strategy3D keeps spec and the four deferred methods. The matcher takes the shift increment for the sigma2 update as the stored shift after srch minus the stored shift before it: s%prev_shvec was that stored shift (prep4srch and prep4prob set it from the project record, and every polar strategy calls one of them for a particle of positive state). For a rejected particle the old increment was the shift itself and the new one is zero; its only reader, calc_sigma2, skips state-zero particles. strategy3D_srch writes cont_inpl_attempted and cont_inpl_improved at the end of its two continuous routes (refine_selected_continuously, refine_assignment_continuously) under inpl_cont=yes, where the matcher clears both fields for every particle before the loop, so a particle whose search runs no route keeps zeros as before.

As built in Phase 7. simple_strategy3D_cont holds strategy3D_cont, which extends strategy3D directly and has the four methods only; the module also exports the pure cont_seed_is_valid (positive state, eo 0 or 1, a projection direction, finite Euler angles and shift; the identity is valid), which srch turns into a stop. new validates the policy (oritype=ptcl3D, objfun euclid or cc, inpl_cont=no, projrec not yes) and builds one cartft_pose_opt from box, box_crop, trs, athres and pose_cont_route. srch rejects a state-zero particle, finds the particle's slot in build%cftc by particle index (get_ptcl_slot; the matcher calls set_ptcl_inds after each batch build, the polar calculator's pinds), runs one refine transaction, takes corr_cart as the calculator's score of the final objective (the seed objective after a rejection), records the residual at the committed pose through the sigma owner under euclid, and calls oris_assign. oris_assign commits the pose only on acceptance, always writes corr_cart and the improved flag, and writes dist, dist_inpl, shincarg, mi_proj, mi_state (1) and frac (100) from the seed-to-result motion; it never writes corr.

docs.title: 6.4 Shared owners
docs.text:
Concern Owner after the refactor Reference handoff materialize_reprojection_model_from_volumes, read_reprojection_model, remove_ref_section_files produce, read and remove the prepared Cartesian reference volumes beside the polar reprojection model; the file contract is section 6.6 Particle preparation A Cartesian sibling of prepimg4align in simple_matcher_2Dprep; build_batch_particles3D fills the active calculator from the single read Per-thread storage prep_strategy3D / clean_strategy3D sigma2 euclid_sigma2 gains a Cartesian calc_sigma2 variant taking cartft_calc, called under euclid only; set_particle_contribution is removed Representation switch One derived logical in parameters (l_cart_refine), set once from refine; no string comparisons downstream Reporting Per-particle fields read by simple_convergence; no stats module, no stats files, no timers in the particle loop

As built in Phase 6. One read prepares a batch for the representation(s) of the pass: build_batch_particles3D(params, build, n, pinds, imgs, imgs_pad) fills the Cartesian slots of build%cftc (a Cartesian pass, or the in-matcher polish until Phase 9) and the polar particles unless l_cart_refine; the Cartesian slots come first, from thread copies, because the polar preparation normalizes the images in place. The Cartesian sibling of prepimg4align is prepimg4align_cart in simple_matcher_2Dprep (the image steps, explicit inputs); the parallel loop, one slot per iteration, is prep_cart_batch in simple_matcher_ptcl_batch, low level (calculator and arrays, so N11, N12 test it without a project), fed by the project's shifts, CTF parameters, noise mask and, under euclid only, sigma2. The calculator cannot run it itself: it would import the matcher layer. build%cftc holds the slots of one batch (new_ptcls). The raw-particle workspace, the _cartesian batch builder and the optional pad-image arguments are gone. euclid_sigma2 has one generic new (the polar constructor shares the table with pftc, a Cartesian pass builds it alone) and one generic calc_sigma2 (polar orientation, or a Cartesian slot at the committed pose); the setter is removed and prep_sigmas_objfun takes no flag; a Cartesian cc pass builds no sigma2 state (C5, N13). prep_strategy3D allocates nothing and the strategy3D toolbox no in-plane table under l_cart_refine. The in-matcher polish evaluates the slot prepared with the batch, centred on the shift stored before the discrete search, as prepimg4align centres the polar particle; its seed is the winner's shift relative to that centring. Before Phase 6 it prepared a second observation centred on the winner's shift, so the polish's mask and taper sit at the pre-search position now (a sub-pixel difference; the scheduled polish of Phase 9 prepares at the winner).

docs.title: 6.5 User-facing surface
docs.text:
• refine=cont in refine3D (replaces refine=pose_cont); in refine3D_auto the switch O7 settles (recommended: pose_cont=only).
  • pose_cont=yes|no schedules a Cartesian pass after every discrete iteration (C19).
  • Removed: pose_cont_mode, pose_cont_route, the program refine3D_pose_cont, the forced cc_emit_sigma=yes.

As built in Phase 8 (O7 (b) adopted). refine3D offers refine=cont (and refine3D_nano, whose refine list is its own) and pose_cont=yes|no; refine3D_auto offers pose_cont=no|yes|only and no refine. parameters holds pose_cont as no|yes|only, only accepted on refine3D_auto alone; l_cart_refine is refine=cont. Validation under refine=cont (validate_parameter_consistency): oritype=ptcl3D on refine3D itself (its children, assembly and postprocessing on other segments, inherit refine with the command line, and the strategy's new checks the segment of the pass), objfun_den=yes rejected (C21), pose_cont=yes rejected (the polish schedules a refine=cont pass; cont is that pass), and inpl_cont overridden to no: the polar in-plane polish is part of the five-parameter solve, and rejecting the default yes would make every refine=cont command line name inpl_cont=no. Initialized poses are a project property, not a parameter: check_cont_seeds (simple_strategy3D_cont) runs at the entry of both refine3D strategies, before the random-orientation fallback for an unsearched field, and at the entry of refine3D_auto pose_cont=only. objfun=cc with refine=cont stays available through refine3D (C20); refine3D_auto sets objfun=euclid as before. Until Phase 9 pose_cont=yes stopped with a message in refine3D (reject_matcher_polish) and in refine3D_auto; from Phase 9 it schedules the polish (checkpoint 7).

docs.title: 6.6 Prepared reference volumes: the handoff file contract
docs.text:
The Cartesian path hands the matcher volumes, not projections. For each state and half the file holds the prepared real-space volume, the one the polar branch pads and reprojects over its grid. The calculator pads and transforms it once when it reads it and gathers each Fourier sample at the continuous rotation during the solve (section 6.2).

Why a file at all: the preparation (volume choice, masking, filtering, envelope, low-resolution even/odd blend, centering with its shift mapped into the project) and the band limit (set_bp_range3D, estimate_lp_from_refs) are decided once, by the iteration strategy, before any matcher runs (refine3D_policy.md, section 6). Every matcher of the iteration, shared-memory or distributed, then reads the same references and the same band. With pose_cont=yes the discrete and the Cartesian passes of one iteration see one preparation by construction.

Alternative not taken (C22): each matcher prepares its references from the state volumes. The preparation and the band-limit decision would then run once per partition; the band limit and the centering shift would need another channel to the workers (the project mutation of centering must stay on the master); and the polar and Cartesian references of one iteration would come from two preparations. It saves a file of nstates * box_crop^3 * 4 bytes per half, written once and read once per partition, far less than the particle images each partition reads.

The layout follows the polar reprojection model (reprojection_model_even.bin and _odd.bin: a four-integer header, then the payload, validated by reprojection_model_header_compatible). The handoff itself is settled (C22); the layout below is confirmed before Phase 4 starts (review checkpoint 3).

Item Contract Files cart_refvols_even.bin, cart_refvols_odd.bin, named by refine3D_cart_refvols_fname(half) in simple_refine3D_fnames. They replace the per-state pose_cont_reference_stateNN_*.mrc files. Layout Stream binary. Header: five default integers [format_version, box_crop, nstates, kfrom, kto] and one default real smpd_crop. Payload: nstates real-space volumes of box_crop^3 default reals, state 1 first, each the prepared reference that the polar branch pads and reprojects. Version format_version = 1. A reader rejects any other value. Compatibility on read box_crop and nstates equal the run's; smpd_crop equal within single-precision tolerance; 1 <= kfrom <= kto <= fdim(box_crop) - 1; the even and odd headers are identical. The checks are a logical function, cart_refvols_header_compatible, which the reader calls; on a mismatch the reader stops the run and names the file and the field. Band limit The reader sets params%kfromto and params%lp from the header, as adopt_reprojection_model_range does for the polar model. No other source of kfromto exists in a Cartesian pass. Producer materialize_reprojection_model_from_volumes, through cartft_calc%write, from the volumes it has just prepared in memory. It writes after preparation has succeeded, replacing the previous files, as it does for the polar model. With pose_cont=yes the same call writes the polar reprojection model and these volumes from one preparation. Reader read_reprojection_model, through cartft_calc%read, in the matcher. Shared-memory and distributed runs read the same files. Removal remove_ref_section_files. Nothing else deletes them. Size On disk nstates * box_crop^3 * 4 bytes per half (67 MB per state at box_crop 256). In the matcher each volume becomes its padded transform, about eight times that (section 6.2).

The alternative layout keeps one MRC volume per state and half, which can be opened in a viewer, with a small header file beside them for the band limit. It needs a completeness check across several files where the single file needs none.

As built in Phase 4 (the layout above, as written; review checkpoint 3 in section 15). The calculator owns the format: set_refvol(state, iseven, volume) stages a prepared volume without a transform (the materializer needs no padded reference), write(fname_even, fname_odd, kfromto, smpd) writes both files and refuses a header the reader would reject, read(fname_even, fname_odd, nstates, box, nptcls, smpd, kfromto) builds the calculator, checks both headers with cart_refvols_header_compatible (type-bound, against the calculator's box and state count; it names the first failing field, which the reader prints with both file names before it stops) and returns the header's band. The file names come from the caller (refine3D_cart_refvols_fname), so the calculator knows no workflow naming. builder%cftc holds the calculator. In simple_matcher_refvol_utils, read_mask_filter_reproject_refvols stages the volumes of every state in build%cftc when a Cartesian pass reads them (l_cart_refine, or the in-matcher polish pose_cont=yes until Phase 7) and skips the polar model under l_cart_refine (its cartesian_only argument is gone); materialize_reprojection_model_from_volumes removes the previous files after the preparation has succeeded and writes the polar model unless l_cart_refine and the reference volumes when they are read; read_reprojection_model dispatches to read_cart_refvols under l_cart_refine, which reads build%cftc with one particle slot per thread (the forwarders' slots until Phase 6) and adopts kfromto and lp as adopt_reprojection_model_range does. The matcher of a Cartesian pass reads at entry, where the polar pass adopts its band, because an empty partition's sigma2 output needs the band before any reference is used; the polish reads the volumes after the polar model. l_cart_refine is derived once in parameters (refine=pose_cont until Phase 8 renames the value).

docs.title: 7.1 Stages
docs.text:
Stage of exec_refine3D_auto Today With refine=cont Hard default refine=prob_neigh Always set Derived from the switch of O7: refine=cont (recommended: from pose_cont=only) Sampling (nsample, update_frac, trail_rec) Set from the active particle count Unchanged (C12) ref_pose_init=cc Optional polar CC pose initialization Bypassed; the combination is rejected Sigma bootstrap (calc_pspec) and startup reconstruct3D Run Run; neither is polar NU low-pass seeding Run Run Registration pass (refine=greedy, polar) On by default (regpass) Bypassed Main loop refine=prob_neigh, nspace, nspace_sub, prob_align, polar reprojection model refine=cont; no projection grid, no probability tables, no polar model Final reconstruction (calc_final_rec) Run Run

This is a continuation mode (C11). It does not produce poses; it refines the ones a discrete workflow left in the project (abinitio3D, or a polar refine3D_auto or refine3D run). The commander checks this at entry, before the sigma bootstrap, with the existing seed check (positive state, half-set assignment, finite Euler angles and shifts for every active particle), and stops with a message that names the requirement. The UI text of the switch (O7) on refine3D_auto says the same.

set_refine3D_auto_sampling stays as it is. Because refine=cont is not a probabilistic mode, the matcher draws the sample itself through sample_ptcls4update3D (update-count sampling under balance=no).

As built in Phase 8. exec_refine3D_auto rejects refine on its command line, reads pose_cont (default no) and, for only, rejects an explicit ref_pose_init=cc or regpass=yes, sets regpass=no and refine=cont, runs check_cont_seeds on ptcl3D right after params%new (before the sampling, the startup volume and the sigma bootstrap), removes pose_cont from the command line its children receive, and runs the main loop with refine=cont and no nspace/nspace_sub. The iteration strategy needs no branch of its own: refine=cont is not a probabilistic mode, so no prob_align child runs, and materialize_reprojection_model_from_volumes writes only the Cartesian reference volumes under l_cart_refine (Phase 4). The final reconstruction (calc_final_rec) is unchanged as the table says: when it must rebuild sigma2 at native sampling (box changed, or no valid committed state), bootstrap_rec3D runs its residual pass with refine=sigma through the polar matcher. That is reconstruction-side sigma estimation after the refinement, not a search; the exit's "no polar model" is checked on the refinement iterations (N20 stage e).

docs.title: 7.2 Convergence (open, O2)
docs.text:
• The single-state rule in check_conv3D is frac_srch%avg > 99 .and. mi_proj > overlap, gated by minits. refine3D_auto sets overlap=0.99.
  • Per particle, mi_proj is 1 when the symmetry-aware angular distance between the previous and the new orientation is at most angthres_mi_proj (default 2 degrees). It is not tied to the discrete grid.
  • A local optimizer reports frac=100, as deterministic neighbourhood refinement already does, so the frac gate is always met.
  • Under refine=cont the rule therefore reduces to "99% of the updated particles moved less than 2 degrees", which a pass that only removes grid error could meet at once, and it ignores shifts.
  • Precedent for a motion-based rule: 2D refine=inpl converges on dist_inpl%avg < 0.5.

Interim rule until O2 is decided: check_conv3D does not declare convergence under refine=cont. A run goes to maxits, which refine3D_auto derives from the target number of updates per particle. minits would only delay the faulty decision. With pose_cont=yes in a discrete mode the rule is unchanged, because the polish leaves the discrete search's convergence fields in place (Phase 9).

Candidates to evaluate on the logged statistics: an angular threshold derived from the current resolution and mask diameter (the registration pass already computes res / (mskdiam/2)); a rule on mean orientation and shift motion (dist, shincarg); the fraction of improved particles falling below a floor (an FSC plateau was listed here; ruling R5 removes the FSC from validation).

docs.title: 9. Phases
docs.text: Each phase is one reviewable change that compiles and passes the fast gate. Stop for maintainer review at every phase boundary. The tests named in each phase are defined in section 10.

docs.title: Phase 0. Baseline
docs.text:
• Everything is recorded at the branch point, the commit the refactoring branches from, not at 712b4d86. 30d23bc62 changed padding handling in read, the backward transform and the normalizations, all on the particle and reference preparation path; whether the Cartesian numbers moved is not known, and a baseline at the branch point makes the question moot.
  • Recorded from the test entries (needs no user data): results and per-sub-suite times of unit_cart_align3D and lib_cart_align3D; the fast-gate timing table (ctest_fast.log.timing.txt); the truth metrics of simulated_workflow_1jxy, simulated_workflow_6vxx and abinitio3D_addon, which section 10.5 compares against (metrics.tsv where the entry writes one, today abinitio3D_addon; otherwise the volume-correlation and FSC lines of its log).
  • Recorded by the maintainer on the beta-gal set: one refine3D refine=pose_cont iteration and one pose_cont=yes iteration (FSC, mean motion, accept fraction, peak RSS, wall time) for both LM routes; one ordinary refine3D_auto run with continuous refinement off.
  • From the lib_cart_align3D run (E25), record the metrics that later serve as pre-refactor floors: rotation and shift error before and after, accept fraction, mean objective before and after, and the truth-map correlation of the perturbed and refined reconstructions. Where the tester computes a metric without printing it, a print line is added; no assertion changes.
  • Record the files each run leaves in its directory.

Exit: numbers and file inventories pasted into section 15.

docs.title: Phase 1. Remove the separate program (C13)
docs.text:
• Delete the commander, the workflow module and its tester, the UI file, the exec case and the policy file; drop the paragraph of refine3D_auto_policy.md that links to that policy file.
  • Remove pose_cont_mode from parameters, the parser and validation, including the program-name checks in parameters_phases (lines 853-863) and the prg case at line 821.
  • Remove the four hooks from commander_refine3D_auto and restore the inline defaults, registration-pass setup and main-stage call.
  • Tests: retire E22-E24 and E26 (section 10.2).

Exit: exec_refine3D_auto differs from e86286f2^ only by unrelated later commits; the ordinary refine3D_auto baseline reproduces; registry check clean.

docs.title: Phase 2. Numerical owners (C3, C17)
docs.text:
• The first commit is the two public interfaces: type definitions, public procedure signatures and their doc comments, no bodies. Review checkpoint 1 is held on that commit, before code moves behind it.
  • Create cartft_calc and cartft_pose_opt by moving code without changing formulas, defaults or the current objective. Both LM routes stay.
  • Private components, new/kill, type-bound methods. Replace error stop with THROW_HARD for caller-contract violations and typed statuses for per-particle failures. THROW_HARD is not callable from a pure procedure: the checks in sample_fourier_with_grad and the two shift conversions become a status returned to the non-pure caller, or move to that caller.
  • Keep simple_cartesian_pose_refiner and the adapter compiling as thin forwarders so production is untouched; they gain no behavior.
  • Tests: the refiner and adapter testers keep running unchanged against the forwarders, which is the parity proof. Their checks (E4-E19) are copied to the calculator and optimizer testers and run against the new interfaces; port E25; add N1 and N2.

Exit: every Phase 0 numerical result reproduces within the existing tolerances through both the old and the new testers; neither class imports matcher, commander, UI or project modules.

docs.title: Phase 3. Objectives follow objfun (C4, C5, C6)
docs.text:
The scientific change, reviewed on its own.

  • Dispatch on params%cc_objfun; implement the cc and euclid definitions of section 5; remove POSE_CONT_OBJECTIVE_* and the cc_emit_sigma override in parameters_phases. Particle preparation under cc no longer requires valid sigma2 shells: sigma2 enters the euclid path only (C5).
  • Shell membership by nint(r) (section 5).
  • Apply the rulings on O4 (particle preparation), O5 (particle-side interpolation) and O6 (search bounds). Under the recommendations the observation is centred, flipped and masked as prepimg4align prepares it, carries the stencil's taper, and is solved for a shift increment within trs and a rotation within athres.
  • Tests: rewrite E8 and E15 for the new definitions; retire E20; add N3-N7 and N28; run E25 under each objective, with floors from the injected error and the Phase 0 values (section 10.1), not from its own first run, and add its high-resolution case (section 10.3).

Exit: both objectives pass formula, gradient and recovery tests; N6 shows the Cartesian and polar objectives select the same grid pose; the high-resolution E25 case meets its floors.

docs.title: Phase 4. Builder and reference handoff (C10, C22)
docs.text:
• Add builder%cftc; derive l_cart_refine once in parameters.
  • Implement the file contract of section 6.6: write/read on the calculator, a logical header-compatibility function, the calls from the reference materializer and reader, the filename function, and removal in remove_ref_section_files.
  • Delete new_inverse_envelope_reference (kept instead if O5 is ruled (b)).
  • Tests: retire E6; keep E10 as the guard on the gather; add N8 and N9.

Exit: one owner produces, validates, reads and removes the references; a distributed worker builds the calculator from declared files only; no file I/O in the optimizer.

docs.title: Phase 5. Representation-neutral strategy base (C17)
docs.text:
• Move s from strategy3D to a new abstract strategy3D_pftc; change the parent of the nine polar strategies.
  • Matcher: shift increment from the project orientation before and after srch; cont_inpl_* written by strategy3D_srch.
  • Tests: unit_pftc_align2D3D unchanged; add N10; rerun the Phase 0 polar guards (section 10.5).

Exit: ordinary refine3D and refine3D_auto baselines reproduce; the matcher contains no ptr%s.

docs.title: Phase 6. Shared helpers select the representation
docs.text:
• build_batch_particles3D prepares the active calculator's particles from the single read; remove build_batch_particles3D_cartesian, the particle workspace argument and the optional pad-image arguments.
  • prep_sigmas_objfun and euclid_sigma2: Cartesian calc_sigma2, under euclid only; a cc pass allocates, reads and writes no sigma2 (C5); remove cartesian_only.
  • prep_strategy3D / clean_strategy3D and the builder toolbox allocate only what the active representation needs.
  • Tests: move E13 (observation part) and E18 to their new owners; add N11-N14 and N26.

Exit: no shared helper imports a continuous-pose module or takes a feature flag; one sigma path; N14 passes.

docs.title: Phase 7. strategy3D_cont and matcher cut-over (C1, C2, C14, C15)
docs.text:
• Implement strategy3D_cont on the Phase 2-6 objects: seed from the project field, one solve against the particle's state and half reference, commit pose and corr_cart together, write corr_cart at the seed when the solve is rejected, leave corr untouched (C14), sigma through the sigma owner under euclid only (C5), convergence fields (dist, dist_inpl, shincarg, mi_proj, frac).
  • Matcher: the strategy case and nothing else; remove every entry of section 8.1. The in-matcher polish is unavailable from here until Phase 9.
  • Delete the adapter, the old strategy, the stats module, the forwarders of Phase 2, the master-side stats aggregation, and their testers.
  • Record layout of O8: under the recommendation the width stays 52, slot 51 becomes corr_cart and slot 52 stays the improved flag; simple_convergence derives attempted from sampled and reports the score of a Cartesian pass from corr_cart, of a polar pass from corr.
  • Tests: delete the old refiner and adapter testers with the forwarders (their checks already run in the calculator and optimizer testers); retire E21; move the seed-validity check of E19 to the strategy3D_cont tester; port E25 to strategy3D_cont; add N15-N19 and N27.

Exit: the matcher's only continuous-pose symbol is strategy3D_cont; no select type; ordinary refinement baselines reproduce.

docs.title: Phase 8. refine=cont surface and refine3D_auto (C7, C11, C12, C16, C18, C20, C21)
docs.text:
• UI and parameters: the refine value becomes cont; refine3D_auto gets the switch O7 settles (recommended: pose_cont=no|yes|only, refine derived and rejected on its command line); pose_cont_route is removed and the kept LM route becomes private; validation in validate_parameter_consistency (oritype=ptcl3D, initialized poses, inpl_cont interaction, C20, C21).
  • simple_refine3D_strategy: for refine=cont, no prob_align child and no polar model.
  • exec_refine3D_auto: section 7.1, including the entry check that makes it a continuation mode.
  • Convergence: no early stop under refine=cont (section 7.2); mean orientation motion, mean shift motion, improved fraction and resolution are logged every iteration.
  • Tests: reduce the route tests E16 and E17 to the kept route; add N20 (stages a-e and h), N21, N25 and the refine=cont stage of N29.

Exit: refine3D_auto in continuous-only mode (O7) completes from a project whose poses came from a polar run, runs to maxits, updates nsample particles per iteration, and creates no polar model, probability table or registration pass; shared-memory and distributed runs agree.

docs.title: Phase 9. Polish as a scheduled pass (C8, C9, C19)
docs.text:
• pose_cont=yes makes the iteration strategy follow every discrete pass with a refine=cont pass over the same particle sample (sample4update_reprod), in refine3D and in the main loop of refine3D_auto.
  • One reconstruction per iteration, from the polished poses: the discrete pass writes no partial reconstructions when a polish follows.
  • The polish pass writes pose, corr_cart, the improved flag and, under euclid, sigma; corr keeps the discrete pass's value. It leaves the convergence fields of the discrete search (dist, dist_inpl, mi_proj, frac) in place, so the main-loop convergence rule keeps measuring the discrete search and is not met trivially by the small polish motion.
  • Tests: add N22 and N23; extend N20 with stages f and g; add the pose_cont=yes stage of N29.

Exit: with pose_cont=no every baseline reproduces; with pose_cont=yes the pose error against the simulation truth is no worse than without it, and a discrete iteration that follows a polish runs unaffected.

docs.title: Phase 10. Documentation and closing checks
docs.text:
• Add the continuous-pose section to doc/policies/3D/refine3D_policy.md and refine3D_auto_policy.md.
  • Update doc/policies/test_environment_policy.md: the sub-suite table of section 1.1, the long-running table of 1.2, the process budget, and the "Where is my test now?" table.
  • Regenerate doc/code_overview/fortran-indexes once, here.
  • SIMPLE_UNIT_ORDER=reverse simple_test_exec test=unit_cart_align3D.

Exit: stale-symbol scan empty for pose_cont_refine3D_adapter, pose_cont_run_stats, strategy3D_pose_cont, cartesian_pose_refiner, pose_cont_mode, pose_cont_route, refine3D_pose_cont; this file moves to doc/refactoring_notes/completed/.

docs.title: 10.1 Principles
docs.text:
From doc/policies/test_environment_policy.md:

  • A test asserts through simple_test_utils, derives its expected value independently of the code under test, names its tolerances, fixes its seeds, and pins sign, handedness and index conventions.
  • A unit test is a routine in simple_<thing>_tester.f90 beside the code it tests, exporting one run_all_<thing>_tests, registered as a sub-suite in simple_commanders_test_class.f90 and listed in the suite= help of simple_test_ui_class.f90.
  • Fast tier: hermetic, in-process, one thread, each sub-suite well under a second, whole gate under 30 s. Library tier: the same rules at realistic size. High-level tier: a pipeline on simulated data, gated against the simulation truth with declared floors and a metrics.tsv.
  • A new CTest entry is an owner decision; the one new entry of this plan is accepted (C18).

Specific to this refactoring:

  • An existing test is moved, not rewritten, when its guarantee still holds. It moves in the same commit as the code it tests.
  • While a forwarder exists (Phases 2-6), the old tester keeps running against it. That is the parity proof for the move.
  • A test is retired only when its subject is deleted or its guarantee is replaced by a decision in section 3. The commit names the reason and the replacing test.
  • A new behavior is not complete until its test is in the same phase. No phase exits on manual inspection alone.
  • Cross-representation tests compare optima and physical quantities, never raw objective values (C9).
  • A floor is never taken from the first run of the code being accepted. It comes from the simulation truth (the error must fall by a stated factor relative to the injected error), from an analytic bound (the rotation error must end below the basin width at the band limit, lp / (mskdiam/2) radians), or from the pre-refactor implementation measured at Phase 0 on the same fixture, with a stated margin.
  • Ruling R5 (2026-10-01, recorded in Phase 8; amended the same day, recorded in Phase 10): the FSC counts only at a scale where it means something. For small tests on noisy particles (2 000 particles or fewer, E25 at 1 000, the N20 gate, N29) the FSC is no criterion; correctness is verified against the ground-truth orientations (rotation and shift error, RMS and median, before and after; fraction within the basin width; accept fraction), and every FSC floor, FSC comparison with Phase 0 and FSC-triggered rerun is dropped for them, including the FSC entries of E25's floors and of any polar guard of 2 000 particles or fewer. At larger scale (more than 2 000 particles) the FSC may serve as a criterion where the plan uses one: to the truth on simulated data, the half-map FSC on the beta-gal set (5 513 particles). Existing CTest entries keep their own built-in checks. E25 keeps its map-correlation floors and its check that the FSC curves are finite; it has no FSC floor. Phases 8 and 9 applied the first wording, which drops the FSC everywhere; their beta-gal FSC values are in their logs and are compared with Phase 0 in the Phase 10 row.
  • A guarantee that ends in THROW_HARD cannot be asserted in-process. Such checks are written as logical functions that the caller turns into a stop, and the function is what the test asserts.
  • Fixtures stay at the sizes already in use (box 16 and 24 in the fast tier) and any file is named tmp_<tester>_* and removed, also on failure.

As built in Phase 8 (commander_test_cont_refine3D_1jxy, floors declared in the code and here before the first run).
